Cas de maladie digestive à Kébémer : les précisions du ministère de la Santé
items.description: Le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique a fait état de 56 cas de maladie digestive notifiés entre le 2 et le 4 novembre 2026 dans le district sanitaire de Kébémer, dans la région de Louga, précisant que 42 patients ont été hospitalisés et qu’aucun décès n’a été enregistré. Dans un communiqué rendu public jeudi, le ministère indique que les personnes concernées présentaient notamment des diarrhées, des vomissements, des douleurs abdominales et, dans certains cas, de la fièvre. Il précise que l’état de santé global des patients est stable et que toutes les personnes concernées ont été prises en charge par les équipes sanitaires. Selon les premières observations, cet épisode pourrait être lié à une toxi-infection d’origine alimentaire ou hydrique. Des investigations approfondies sont en cours pour en déterminer les causes exactes. Elles sont menées par des équipes mixtes de la Direction régionale de la Santé de Louga et de la Direction de la Prévention, en appui aux équipes du district sanitaire de Kébémer. Le ministère assure suivre de près l’évolution de la situation et promet de tenir régulièrement informée la population de toute évolution significative. Il appelle également les populations à faire preuve de vigilance, à respecter les recommandations sanitaires en vigueur et à se référer aux informations diffusées par les sources officielles. S.G

items.title: Saudi Arabia executes five Ethiopians for hashish smuggling
items.description: Saudi Arabia has executed five Ethiopian nationals convicted of drug smuggling, bringing the kingdom’s execution toll this year to 205, according to the country’s Interior Ministry. The five were convicted of participating in smuggling hashish into the kingdom, the ministry said in a statement published by the official Saudi Press Agency on Thursday. They were executed in Asir, a province in southwestern Saudi Arabia. The latest executions are the third such announcement involving Ethiopian nationals in recent months. Five Ethiopians were executed on the same day in June, while another five were put to death in July. With the latest executions, 32 Ethiopian nationals have been executed in Saudi Arabia this year, making them the largest foreign national group among those executed. Human Rights Watch warned in July that at least 79 Ethiopians faced an imminent risk of execution over similar drug-related charges. Saudi Arabia recorded 356 executions last year, the highest annual figure in the kingdom’s history. Thousands of Ethiopians work in low-skilled jobs in Saudi Arabia, with many travelling to the oil-rich kingdom through the perilous Eastern Route from the Horn of Africa via Yemen. items.title: Gadi Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government with backing of Arab lists
items.description: Israel’s largest Arab list on Thursday said it would back Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, bolstering his chances of being picked over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who lost the support of an allied religious party. President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultation s with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority. Herzog will himself choose whom to ask to form a new government, but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parties, which would be Eisenkot. Arab-majority lists won an unprecedented 19 seats in the election, making them potential kingmakers if Eisenkot’s opposition chooses to work with them — something which remains unclear. Both Arab lists on Thursday said they were backing Eisenkot. The Joint List, which bagged 11 seats, said in a statement that “it will inform Herzog this evening of its decision to recommend that Gadi Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government”. Raam, which won eight seats, also endorsed Eisenkot. Ultra-Orthodox exemptions Meanwhile, United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot. The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government”, the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats. Alongside Shas, another ultra-Orthodox party, they have pushed to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis, as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza , Lebanon and Iran . “In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students,” United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said. Eisenkot, who has tried to appeal to secular Israelis from left to right, has been adamant about ending exemptions from military service. Some of his opposition allies have criticised the ultra-Orthodox — who make up about 14 per cent of the population but have far higher birthrates than secular Israelis — as a drain on the state. Observers say United Torah Judaism’s tactic is likely aimed mostly at punishing Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they would still serve in a government if he were to form one. Arab parties play key role Once Herzog gives his mandate to a lawmaker, the person will have 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension. If the lawmaker fails, Herzog will then task someone else. Netanyahu’s bloc, including United Torah Judaism, has 53 seats in the new parliament, compared to 48 for Eisenkot’s bloc. Arab-majority parties scored historic gains on the back of anger over Netanyahu’s hard-right government, whose ministers have vowed to treat Arab Israelis much like Palestinians in war-ravaged Gaza and the occupied West Bank. Eisenkot could form a government with the Arab parties’ numbers but would risk losing support from some in the opposition, notably Avigdor Liberman, a former Netanyahu aide turned outspoken critic, who nonetheless shares the outgoing government’s hawkish views on the Palestinians. Netanyahu has relentlessly attacked the opposition for even the prospect of an alliance with Arab lawmakers. In a video on Wednesday filmed in the prime minister’s office, Netanyahu alleged there were “serious suspicions” that foreign powers put money into the election and questioned the loyalty of Arab citizens.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : des médailles et des compétitions à l'affiche de la quatrième journée des jeux
items.description: Pour leur quatrieme journee, le 4 novembre, les jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) de Dakar 2026 ont concocte un tres beau lot de competitions et de medailles aussi aux jeunes athletes participants au premier evenement olympique en Afrique. Plusieurs sportifs se sont distingues en beach-volley, skateboard et natation. L'Autriche et les Pays-Bas obtiennent l'or en beach-volley L'equipe masculine autrichienne de beach-volley, composee de Paul Hohenauer et de Martin Poinstingl, est montee sur la premiere marche du podium en s'imposant face a la paire allemande Lasse Hüper et Filo Wüst, qui a termine deuxieme, alors que la medaille de bronze est revenue aux Australiens Ryan Edgar et Thomas Turner. Dans le tournoi feminin, l'or est alle aux Neerlandaises Jara Both et Matilda de Groot face aux Italiennes Micol Lafuente et Margaritha Coretti, qui ont remporte l'argent, tandis que les Suissesses Noemi Eugster et Anja Gaehwiler ont pris la troisieme place. Une medaille d'or pour la Russie et pour l'Afrique en natation Le Japon a domine les epreuves masculines et feminines de natation du 200 m 4 nages grâce a la victoire de Iori Miyazaki, qui a remporte l'or chez les hommes. Idem pour sa compatriote Mana Ishikawa, montee sur le podium. L'egypte a encore decroche l'or pour l'Afrique grâce a la performance de Zain Ali sur 50 m papillon, alors que la Russe Serafima Fokina s'est imposee dans la meme discipline pour les femmes. Sur 50 m nage libre, l'or est revenu au Tcheque et a la Croate, sacres chacun dans sa categorie. Un Americain champion olympique de skateboard Pour les epreuves de skateboard, qui comptent parmi les sports olympiques depuis les Jeux de Tokyo en 2021, l'Americain Julian Jeangagliardi a remporte la finale masculine du street avec 149,37 points, devant le Neerlandais Tijmen Overbeek et le Suisse Simon Gerber, qui ont pris respectivement l'argent et le bronze. Le Japon, la Chine et la Russie au top 3 du classement des medailles Le Japon mene, pour le moment, le classement des medailles pour les JOJ de Dakar 2026 avec sept medailles d'or, deux d'argent et trois de bronze. La Chine est au second rang avec cinq medailles d'or, trois d'argent et deux de bronze. La Russie suit avec trois medailles d'or et deux d'argent. L'egypte occupe pour sa part le quatrieme rang mondial et le premier rang africain avec trois medailles d'or et une medaille de bronze. Le Senegal, pays hote, figure aussi au tableau des medailles grâce au bronze de Matar Diop, remporte lors de l'epreuve de judo dans la categorie des moins de 66 kg.

items.title: Atiku flags off ADC campaign in Kebbi, pledges security, fuel subsidy restoration
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi BIRNIN KEBBI — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to address Nigeria’s security challenges and restore fuel subsidy if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the promises during the flag-off of his campaign in Kebbi State, where he described the forthcoming election as a referendum on the policies of the President Bola Tinubu administration. He said the election would provide Nigerians with an opportunity to decide whether to retain the current government or embrace an alternative amid concerns over economic hardship and insecurity. Supporters of the ADC converged on the party’s secretariat in Birnin Kebbi to welcome Atiku and other party chieftains ahead of the campaign rally. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, commended party members for attending the gathering despite what he described as intimidation by the state government. Akobundu said the 2027 election would be a referendum on the performance of the Tinubu administration, adding that hunger, insecurity and unemployment would feature prominently in the campaign. The ADC National Chairman, in his remarks, described the party as a moving train that could not be stopped by intimidation. He urged Kebbi residents to vote for Abubakar Malami as governor, Atiku as president and other ADC candidates in the 2027 elections. Atiku and his running mate also criticised some projects being presented as achievements of the Tinubu administration, alleging that they were legacies of the late President Muhammadu Buhari. They described the ADC as an alternative for Nigerians seeking improved security and a reversal of the fuel subsidy policy. The rally climaxed with the ADC National Chairman formally presenting the party’s flag to Malami as its governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Meanwhile, security was heightened in Birnin Kebbi ahead of Atiku’s arrival, with security personnel deployed across parts of the state capital to prevent any breakdown of law and order. The campaign rally ended peacefully, with no reported attacks or destruction of vehicles, unlike the violence alleged to have accompanied the party’s campaign activities in Sokoto State. The post Atiku flags off ADC campaign in Kebbi, pledges security, fuel subsidy restoration appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Two killed, 20 abducted in Kaduna community attack
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — Two persons have reportedly been killed and 20 others abducted after suspected terrorists invaded Akwando community in Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The attackers reportedly stormed the community around noon on Wednesday, shooting residents and abducting several people. The police had yet to officially confirm the incident as of Thursday. The President of the Kuturmi Unity Development Association (KUDA), Dr Joseph Ariko, and its Publicity Secretary, Manasseh Samuel Akwando, disclosed the attack in a statement expressing concern over the security situation in Kuturmi communities. The association said the latest attack had worsened the plight of residents still struggling to recover from previous assaults, particularly the Easter Sunday attack on Ariko community. It described the recurring incidents as a threat to the lives, livelihoods and ancestral heritage of the affected communities. KUDA identified the 20 persons reportedly abducted from Akwando as Usman Galadima, La’a’zarus Genesis, Madalin Markus, Happy Stephen, Lovet Ishaya, Afiniki Irimeya, Amina Ahmadu, Miracle Genesis, Hellen Irimeya and Musa Genesis. Others are Janet Irimeya, Gloria Markus, Zila Stephen, Alis Ahmadu, Haske Ahmadu, Great Isiac, Hanatu Irimeya, Desmon Ishaya, Siam Shagari and Nansy Genesis. The association recalled that the Easter Sunday attack on Ariko reportedly claimed five lives at the scene, while another 17 victims subsequently died in captivity. It also cited an earlier attack on Awon community, during which two persons were reportedly killed and 11 others abducted. According to KUDA, five of those abducted in Awon regained their freedom on November 3, 2026, but one reportedly died the following day. Another victim escaped, while five others allegedly died in captivity. The association said the recurring attacks had forced residents to flee their homes, abandon their farmlands and suspend economic activities for fear of further assaults. It further alleged that armed groups had restricted residents’ access to their ancestral lands, compelling some to pay levies before cultivating their farms or harvesting agricultural produce. However, KUDA said the allegations required independent investigation and urged security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents and identify those responsible. It called on the Federal and Kaduna State governments, as well as the Kachia Local Government Council, to strengthen security in Akwando, Ariko, Awon and other vulnerable communities. Specifically, the association demanded the deployment of adequately equipped security personnel, establishment of permanent security posts, regular patrols and effective early-warning mechanisms to prevent further attacks. It also appealed for coordinated security operations to secure the release of the 20 residents reportedly abducted in Akwando and others still being held captive. KUDA further called for the prosecution of those responsible for the attacks and the provision of humanitarian assistance to displaced residents, survivors and families of victims. The association urged President Bola Tinubu, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, the National Security Adviser, the Inspector-General of Police and the Chief of Defence Staff to intervene, warning that affected communities remained exposed to recurring killings, abductions and displacement. items.title: 2026 CAF WCL: Beline Nyarko scores winner as Ampem Darkoa Ladies beat Kawempe Muslim Ladies
items.description: Ghanaian champions Ampem Darkoa Ladies continued their strong start to the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League following their victory over Kawempe Muslim Ladies. Beline Nyarko scored a late winner for Charles Anokye Frimpon’s side in the 2-1 victory over the Ugandan side to continue their winning streak. The two teams came into the encounter on the back of respective wins over USFAS Bamako and AS FAR in their opening game of the competition. Ampem Darkoa enjoyed a good start to the game and created chances to go ahead. They eventually took the lead in the 19th minute when the opponent’s goalkeeper made a mess out of clearance before Nancy Amoh pounced on the error to open the scoring. The Black Queens midfielder should have doubled the lead moments later, but her decision-making in the final third let her down. Kawempe drew level in the game in the 33rd minute with a miscommunication between Rose Teye Baah and her defender giving the Ugandans the opportunity to equalise. Kawempe dominated possession in the second half of the game but failed to make the most of their dominance. Amepm Darkoa then retook the lead in the 83rd minute when Beline capitalised on another error at the back to give her side the lead. The victory puts the Ghanaians in a good position to advance into the next stage of the comeptition after two wins from their opening two games.

items.title: Power generation drops to 3,659MW as FG explains supply disruptions
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Electricity generation on Nigeria’s national grid dropped to 3,659 megawatts (MW) as of 3pm on Thursday, from a peak of 3,996MW recorded on Wednesday, amid worsening power supply across parts of the country. The Federal Government attributed the decline to gas supply constraints to thermal power plants, reduced water inflows into hydroelectric reservoirs and operational challenges within the power sector. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that the decline had affected electricity allocation to Distribution Companies (DisCos), resulting in shorter hours of supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. Data on the distribution load allocation dashboard as of 5:39pm on Thursday showed that the 11 electricity distribution companies received a combined allocation of 3,031MW. Abuja Disco received the highest allocation of 669MW, followed by Ibadan Disco with 413MW and Port Harcourt Disco with 338MW. Benin Disco received 279MW, Enugu 267MW, Eko 256MW, Ikeja 249MW, Kano 173MW, Kaduna 167MW, Jos 146MW, while Yola Disco received the lowest allocation of 74MW. The Federal Ministry of Power, in a statement on Thursday by the Special Adviser (Media and Publicity) to the Minister of Power, Adeola Adelabu, acknowledged complaints by electricity consumers in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo states over worsening supply in recent days. The Ministry noted that the affected areas had recently experienced noticeable improvements in electricity supply before the latest disruptions. It, however, ruled out a major or systemic failure of the national grid, explaining that preliminary assessments linked the disruptions to maintenance and operational challenges in parts of the power value chain, alongside declining generation. Acknowledging the impact of the disruptions on consumers, the Ministry said: “We recognise what every hour without power means for individuals, families and businesses, and we do not take it lightly.” It added that the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, was working with the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), NISO and electricity distribution companies to address the challenges and restore normal supply. According to the Ministry, the Minister had engaged relevant operators to resolve the operational constraints, accelerate ongoing maintenance and keep the public informed about restoration efforts. In a separate statement, NISO confirmed that limited gas availability had constrained the ability of affected thermal generating stations to operate at their available capacities, while reduced water inflows had affected hydroelectric generation. The system operator stated: “The limited availability of gas has constrained the capacity of affected thermal generating stations to operate at their available levels, while reduced water inflows into reservoirs have impacted the generation capacity of hydroelectric power stations.” NISO explained that the reduction in available generation had affected the volume of electricity allocated to DisCos for distribution to consumers, resulting in increased load shedding. It added that the extent of the impact varied across distribution networks, depending on available generation and the corresponding allocations to individual DisCos. Acknowledging the impact of the generation shortfall on consumers nationwide, NISO said it remained committed to maintaining grid stability and optimising the dispatch of available generation. It stated: “NISO remains committed to maintaining grid stability, optimizing the dispatch of available generation, and ensuring the secure, reliable and efficient operation of the national grid within prevailing operational constraints.” The system operator also disclosed that it was working towards diversifying the country’s energy mix to strengthen security of electricity supply. items.title: Bole-Bamboi: NPP’s 2024 candidate Raphael Kumah eyes parliamentary seat again
items.description: The New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) 2024 parliamentary candidate for Bole-Bamboi, Raphael Abolasom Kumah, has declared his intention to contest the constituency’s parliamentary seat again in the 2028 general elections. Mr Kumah made the declaration on Thursday, November 5, 2026, reflecting on his defeat in the 2024 elections and expressing renewed determination to seek a parliamentary mandate. He acknowledged that the outcome of the previous election was not what he had anticipated but attributed the defeat to what he described as a nationwide political wave that affected constituencies across the country, including Bole-Bamboi. He said the experience had, however, provided valuable lessons and strengthened his resolve to continue pursuing his ambition of serving the people. “Today, with a heart full of hope and renewed determination, I humbly declare my intention to contest in the 2028 Parliamentary Elections,” he said. Mr Kumah said his decision was informed by his conviction that the people of Bole-Bamboi deserved dedicated, accessible and committed leadership capable of delivering meaningful results. He also highlighted the need for a strong working relationship between the constituency’s party leadership and its parliamentary leadership, arguing that cooperation and unity between the two structures would be important to the NPP’s efforts in the 2028 elections. Calls for unity and reconciliation Addressing internal challenges within the party, Mr Kumah acknowledged that there had been lapses in the past but urged members to avoid dwelling on blame and accusations. Instead, he called for a forward-looking approach centred on reconciliation, unity and the collective interest of the constituency. He said the 2028 elections presented an opportunity for the NPP in Bole-Bamboi to rebuild its structures, reconnect with grassroots supporters and work towards a common goal. “Going forward, we must not allow the challenges of yesterday to become obstacles to tomorrow’s opportunities,” he emphasised. The parliamentary hopeful further urged party members and supporters to put aside their differences, stressing that the development and future of the constituency should take precedence over individual interests. Mr Kumah reaffirmed his readiness to pursue the parliamentary contest, expressing optimism about the party’s prospects in the constituency. “The journey continues, the commitment remains unwavering, the determination is stronger. I am ready, I am determined, and I believe 2028 is possible!” he declared. He ended his declaration with the campaign message: “Ready! Prepared! Determined! I believe in 2028!” His announcement marks an early entry into the race for the Bole-Bamboi parliamentary seat ahead of the 2028 general elections, with unity, reconciliation and stronger collaboration within the NPP forming the central themes of his message.

items.title: Largely peaceful marches take place across France as workers stage strike
items.description: Some protesters clashed with police in Paris and Lyon on Thursday during largely peaceful nationwide demonstrations and a one-day strike by some public sector workers in a renewed challenge to President Emmanuel Macron. The protests were attended by several high-profile politicians, including presidential candidates Jean-Luc Melenchon and Raphael Glucksmann. They follow demonstrations over living costs, public services and education that have triggered the worst civil unrest France has seen in years. The interior ministry said 270,000 people had participated in protests around the country so far, excluding Paris, where the main demonstration started in the afternoon. People attend a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of strikes and protests over wages, the cost of living and public services called by French labour unions, and joined by high school and university students calling for better education conditions, in Nantes, France on November 5, 2026. — Reuters “This country needs justice,” Glucksmann told reporters at the start of the Paris march. “We are going to bring the French people back together. We are going to restore public services; we will do … the opposite of what’s taken place in the past 10 years.” In Paris, the mood was festive at the start, featuring a diverse group of participants singing ‘ La Marseillaise ’ and some Carnival-like floats. The Eiffel Tower was shut down by the one-day strike, which was joined by some energy workers and teachers, but there were no major disruptions to transport. But about two hours in, some of the people at the front of the march clashed with police, who fired tear gas. Workers, students join forces to press for change In Lyon, riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters, some of whom were seen shouting anti-police slogans and dressed all in black, with face coverings. The Interior Ministry said the police there had been confronted by several hundred hardcore protesters and that the violence had been contained, although tensions remained high. The unrest comes only five months before a presidential election which could pit far-right candidate Marine Le Pen against hard-left rival Melenchon in a second-round run-off. Macron, who is serving his second term and is unpopular, cannot run again. A man holds an umbrella near a fire, as demonstrators attend a nationwide day of strikes and protests over wages, the cost of living and public services, called by French labour unions and joined by high school and university students calling for better education conditions, in Lyon, France on November 5, 2026. — Reuters “There is a lot of concern about the future, notably the issues of salaries, public services,” said Alice Martinovic, an 18-year-old student participating in the Paris demonstration. “I hope in the upcoming elections the candidates will really think about this movement and include the opinions of young people, of students, who are now joined by a lot of other workers.” School ablaze after fireworks are hurled The interior ministry said people throwing fireworks had caused a fire at a high school near the city of Toulouse in the southwest on Thursday morning, forcing pupils and staff to evacuate the building while firefighters doused the flames. “This criminal behaviour is an absolute scandal,” said Education Minister Edouard Geffray on X. French high school students and other demonstrators had earlier faced off against riot police in Paris as they blocked a street with rubbish bins on Thursday morning. While the demonstrations in Lyon and other cities, including Marseille and Nantes, began in the morning, the main protest march in Paris set off in the afternoon from Place de la Republique. Since riots and looting on October 17 caught security forces off guard, leaving damaged shops and public buildings across the country and fuelling criticism of Macron’s handling of the crisis, French authorities have issued curfews, bans on large gatherings and have required groups to take alternate routes for demonstrations that avoid main boulevards, which trade unions have decried. “The government tried to block the demonstrations. The demonstrations are bigger than ever,” Sophie Binet, head of the CGT trade union, told reporters. She estimated that some 250,000 people were demonstrating across France before the Paris march. “High school students, pensioners, students, workers, all together. Unity wins,” read one banner at the protest in Lyon. Police deploy in large numbers “Our pay has not kept up with inflation,” said Mehdi Dumontroty, a 45-year-old firefighter who was joining the protest in Paris. “What happened this summer proves that we were right when we said we needed more resources to deal with the crisis that we faced,” he said, referring to wildfires exacerbated earlier this year by intense heat waves. French CRS riot police stand in position outside the Lycee Helene Boucher high school during a gathering by high school students in Paris as part of a nationwide day of strikes and protests over wages, the cost of living and public services called by French labour unions, and joined by high school and university students calling for better education conditions, in France on November 5, 2026. —Reuters Around 70,000 police were on duty nationwide, a comparable figure to recent weekends. The French government has defended police tactics while saying any abuses would be investigated. The strike contributed to a reduction in France’s nuclear output early on Thursday and the education ministry said just over 15 per cent of French teaching staff had joined the strike.

items.title: FG begins clearing power equipment stranded since 2014
items.description: By Soni Daniel ABUJA — The Federal Government has begun clearing hundreds of containers of electricity equipment stranded at Nigerian ports for more than a decade, in a move aimed at recovering abandoned public assets and supporting critical power infrastructure projects. The Ministry of Power has secured the release of the first 44 containers from Apapa Port, Lagos, out of more than 300 containers awaiting clearance, some since 2014. The Minister of Power, Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, disclosed this after the recent Federal Executive Council meeting in Abuja. He said the intervention followed President Bola Tinubu’s directive to the ministry to work with the Nigeria Customs Service and the Nigerian Ports Authority to resolve the administrative and financial bottlenecks responsible for the prolonged delay. The bottlenecks, he explained, included the reconciliation of outstanding port charges. “The release of the first 44 containers represents significant progress in our determination to recover critical power assets and accelerate infrastructure development,” the minister said. Tegbe said technical experts would assess the recovered equipment to establish their condition and suitability for deployment. He explained that serviceable equipment would be integrated into ongoing electricity projects, while items considered unserviceable would be appropriately disposed of. The latest exercise follows earlier recovery efforts by the Niger Delta Power Holding Company (NDPHC), under the leadership of its Managing Director, Engr. Jennifer Adighije. The Federal Government said the latest intervention was part of efforts to unlock stranded public investments, strengthen electricity infrastructure and address bottlenecks affecting power delivery across the country. items.title: Ghana urged to integrate universal sickle cell screening into primary healthcare
items.description: Ghana has been urged to establish a sustainable, nationally funded newborn screening programme for sickle cell disease (SCD), building on three decades of progress in early detection and treatment. The call was made by Professor Isaac Odame, Haematology Section Head at the Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) in Toronto, Canada, and Director of the Global Sickle Cell Disease Network, during the inaugural Prof. Ohene-Frempong Memorial Lecture at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital (KBTH) on October 29. The lecture, held in memory of the late Professor Kwaku Ohene-Frempong and his pioneering contribution to sickle cell disease care and research, highlighted Ghana’s achievements in screening and treating the condition since the first pilot newborn screening programme was conducted in Kumasi in 1995. Prof. Odame said Ghana had repeatedly demonstrated the feasibility and benefits of early screening for sickle cell disease, but the initiatives had largely depended on external funding that was limited in duration. He said the country must now move beyond donor-supported projects and commit to a universal screening programme financed and sustained through national resources. According to him, screening infants for sickle cell disease could be incorporated into existing primary healthcare services, including immunisation and child welfare clinics, with the support of newer point-of-care screening technologies. This, he said, would make early diagnosis more accessible and enable affected children to receive appropriate care before complications develop. Early diagnosis key to improving survival Prof. Odame explained that identifying children with sickle cell disease early would allow them to be linked promptly to interventions that could significantly improve their health and quality of life. These include counselling for parents and caregivers, vaccination, penicillin prophylaxis to prevent serious bacterial infections, and hydroxyurea treatment to reduce complications associated with the disease. He stressed the importance of ensuring that screening did not end with diagnosis but was linked to a reliable system of follow-up care and treatment. Demonstration projects offer a pathway for national programme Ghana is already implementing demonstration projects at the Princess Marie Louise Children’s Hospital (PML) and Maamobi General Hospital to identify infants with sickle cell disease and connect them to appropriate care. The projects are providing practical models for integrating early infant screening into routine healthcare delivery and demonstrating how the approach could be expanded across the country’s health system. Prof. Odame said Ghana had an opportunity to build on these initiatives and incorporate sustainable sickle cell disease screening and care into the government’s Free Primary Healthcare Initiative. Such integration, he argued, would help move the country towards a nationally coordinated programme rather than relying on isolated projects whose continuation depends on external financial support. Ghana must build on 30 years of progress The call comes as Ghana marks three decades since the introduction of its first pilot newborn screening programme for sickle cell disease in Kumasi. The next phase, Prof. Odame said, should focus on ensuring that every child born with the condition is identified early and connected to the care needed to live a healthy and productive life. He cited an estimated 16,000 children born with sickle cell disease in Ghana each year, underscoring the scale of the need for a comprehensive national response. He said translating the country’s experience and existing screening models into a sustainable, nationally integrated programme would represent an important step towards health sovereignty. The proposal would require sustained government commitment, reliable financing and the integration of screening, diagnosis and treatment into routine primary healthcare services. It would also help ensure that children born with sickle cell disease are not left undiagnosed or unable to access essential interventions because of where they live or the availability of donor-funded projects.

items.title: JUSAG threatens to withdraw all staff from Supreme Court if strike persists
items.description: The General Secretary of the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG), Abdulai Yakubu, says no judicial service staff at the Supreme Court should report for work if the ongoing strike is not resolved by the end of this week. According to him, the association has instructed its members at the apex court to ensure that Wednesday’s sitting was the last during the industrial action, insisting that judicial service employees should not be made to work while the strike remains in force. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Thursday, November 5, Mr Yakubu said the association was initially surprised when the Supreme Court continued sitting after the strike began. He explained that the leadership engaged its members after the court sat on the first day, believing the situation would be a one-off occurrence. However, he said the leadership was taken by surprise when the Supreme Court sat again on Wednesday. “After the Wednesday sitting, we have given an indication to our members who work at the Supreme Court that let the Wednesday sitting be the last of its kind,” he said. Mr Yakubu clarified that JUSAG was not opposed to the Supreme Court conducting its business but objected to the use of judicial service staff to facilitate court proceedings during the strike. He said there had been no sitting at the Supreme Court on Thursday and indicated that the court might not sit on Friday either. He warned that if the dispute remained unresolved by the close of the week, the association would direct all its members working at the Supreme Court not to report for duty. “If we don’t get any resolution by the close of this week, the message we have for our members who work at the Supreme Court is that no one should turn up at the Supreme Court, and let no management member or anybody coerce any staff to violate any part of this strike,” he said. Mr Yakubu maintained that the strike was protected under international labour laws to which Ghana is a signatory.

items.title: SDP condemns attempts to disqualify ADC presidential candidate, Atiku
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has condemned alleged attempts to disqualify the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, insisting that political parties should be allowed to freely present candidates for the 2027 general elections. The party also called on the judiciary, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remain impartial and protect the country’s democratic process. The SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, stated this on Thursday in Abuja while addressing journalists after a meeting with the party’s nine governorship candidates from different states. Gombe, who said the SDP would not participate in the proposed ‘Rainbow Coalition’, reaffirmed the party’s commitment to contesting the 2027 elections under its own political platform. He also accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of allegedly plotting to infiltrate opposition parties and weaken their ranks ahead of the elections. The SDP chairman alleged that the APC, having lost the confidence of Nigerians over its governance record, was using the proposed coalition to woo opposition members and undermine their unity. He, however, said the SDP was working with other opposition parties towards building a coalition of Nigerians committed to credible elections, including joint training of party agents and the establishment of common situation rooms to protect votes at polling units. Gombe reaffirmed the party’s commitment to presenting what he described as credible alternatives to Nigerians, particularly its presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and vice-presidential candidate, Prof. Usman Bugaje. He said: “I want to assure you that SDP, as a political party, has nothing to do with anything called Rainbow Coalition. “We are with other political parties in the opposition, doing everything possible to rescue our dear country through a coalition of the Nigerian people. “We are not into any Rainbow Coalition where we will have candidates here and profess support for the APC presidency. We are SDP and we are for SDP candidates.” He said the party had resolved to discipline any member who participated in the proposed arrangement without its authorisation. According to Gombe, the meeting with the governorship candidates was part of preparations to strengthen the party’s electoral strategies and improve its chances in the 2027 general elections. He said the engagement provided an opportunity for candidates from different states to share experiences, identify organisational gaps and develop strategies for winning elections at national and state levels. The SDP chairman urged Nigerians to assess the party’s candidates based on their competence, capacity, character and patriotism. He also pledged the party’s commitment to credible elections, saying it would collaborate with other opposition parties on election monitoring, polling agent training and the establishment of joint situation rooms. “We will be our own INEC at the polling units and our own security to ensure free, fair and credible elections come 2027,” he said. Gombe also raised concerns over the alleged failure of INEC to publish the names of some of the party’s candidates, saying the matter was already before the court. He accused the commission of failing to recognise the candidates despite what he described as the party’s compliance with the Electoral Act, the Constitution and its internal nomination procedures. He further condemned what he described as attempts to disqualify Atiku, arguing that political parties should be allowed to freely present candidates for elections. The SDP chairman also expressed concerns over issues relating to the voters’ register and the creation of polling units, warning against actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process. Earlier, the Chairman of the SDP Governors’ Forum and Nasarawa governorship candidate, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, said the meeting was aimed at developing strategies to secure victory in the presidential, governorship and legislative elections. Adamu said the candidates shared experiences from their respective states and discussed ways to address organisational gaps ahead of the polls. He expressed confidence that Nigerians were seeking an alternative to the APC-led government, adding that the SDP would prioritise citizens’ welfare and improved living conditions. The meeting brought together the party’s nine governorship candidates and members of its National Working Committee as part of efforts to strengthen its structures and preparations for the 2027 general elections. The governorship candidates were from Nasarawa, Oyo, Benue, Niger, Adamawa, Plateau, Kano, Gombe and Bauchi states. The post SDP condemns attempts to disqualify ADC presidential candidate, Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Connecting Africa’s wallets, unlocking Africa’s trade, smartly – Gabby Asare Otchere-Darko writes
items.description: Yesterday, Monday, 2 November, I joined discussions at the 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra, including a Smart Africa Steering Committee roundtable. My main message was that connecting Africa’s mobile money wallets across borders, alongside visa-free travel, could transform intra-African trade significantly. At the Africa Prosperity Network (APN), we estimate that implementing both reforms could help raise intra-African trade from around 16% to more than 25% within five years. The opportunity is enormous. The figures I presented show that US$2.1 trillion flowed through mobile money wallets globally in 2025, with approximately US$1.4 trillion, two-thirds of the total, transacted in sub-Saharan Africa. Africa had some 1.2 billion registered accounts, while West Africa alone recorded approximately US$498 billion in transactions across 517 million accounts (not unique individuals). Yet our commercial strength remains constrained by fragmented markets, compared with intra-regional trade figures of approximately 59% in Asia and 68% in Europe. Fragmentation also makes payments for goods and services in intra-African trade expensive. It is estimated that more than 80% of payments between African countries pass through banks outside the continent, with associated payment and currency-conversion arrangements costing Africa approximately US$5.3 billion annually. That is over US$50 billion a decade. Within states, we have built mobile money at an extraordinary scale. Take Ghana, for instance, which was the first to achieve comprehensive mobile money interoperability in 2018. Last August alone, more than one billion mobile money transactions were recorded in a single month. We must now connect those national wallets and put them to work for continental trade, greater opportunities and jobs. Imagine a trader in Kumasi buying from a supplier in Abidjan: she pays in cedis from her wallet, and the supplier receives CFA francs quickly, securely and affordably. Neither needs to source dollars or carry cash across a border. Multiply that transaction across millions of businesses. Lower costs will release money for stock and expansion. Faster settlement will improve cash flow. Reliable transaction records can also support access to credit and insurance. For women, SMEs and young entrepreneurs, this could place Africa’s single market directly in their hands. But a trader who can pay a supplier must also be able to travel to inspect goods, negotiate and build trust, if need be. Free movement and seamless payments should, therefore, go hand in hand. Since the inaugural Africa Prosperity Dialogues in 2023, APN has brought together policymakers, the AfCFTA Secretariat, Smart Africa, GSMA Africa, telecommunications companies and financial institutions to advance this connectivity agenda. The 2024 Peduase Action Compact helped sustain that momentum. At the Sixth AU Mid-Year Coordination Meeting in Accra that July, leaders committed to our outcome document, which essentially focused on working towards wider PAPSS participation, cross-border mobile money interoperability, connected payment channels, common regulatory safeguards and stronger digital infrastructure by 2027. This is what makes the timing and focus of APD 2027, in January, significant. Trusted identity is essential to delivering these ambitions. This is why APN supports the Smart Africa Trust Alliance (SATA) and Smart Africa Data Exchange (SADX). SATA establishes the framework for national identification cooperation, while SADX enables national systems to securely verify and exchange information while countries retain control over their data. Nineteen countries have signed the SATA Declaration. Ghana, Benin and Rwanda have completed the first phase of the SADX pilot, demonstrating cross-border identity verification in a controlled testing environment. We believe this can help address a major obstacle to visa-free travel: governments’ uncertainty about visitors’ identities. Allowing authorised agencies to verify travellers against official records in their home countries, with privacy and security safeguards, could strengthen border management and greatly reduce those concerns. Trusted digital identity can also support access to financial services across borders. We are hopeful because progress is visible. Since our Make Africa Borderless Now! campaign began this year, several countries have introduced or announced visa-free policies for Africans. These sovereign decisions demonstrate growing political willingness to open our borders. Expanding participation in PAPSS and the 19 SATA signatories are equally encouraging. The foundations for freer movement, trusted identities and seamless payments are coming together. With sustained political leadership, regulatory cooperation and industry action, we can achieve significant progress towards continent-wide mobile money interoperability by the end of 2027. A system that allows authorised agencies to verify a visitor’s identity against official records in their home country, with appropriate privacy and security safeguards, could greatly reduce the uncertainty that fuels resistance to visa-free travel. Governments would have greater confidence about who is entering their countries, while traders and other travellers could face fewer delays and obstacles. We believe this can strengthen the political case for opening borders and, over time, support the identity checks needed to access financial services across countries. Connecting Africa’s identities, alongside its wallets, can help build the confidence needed to let our people move freely and trade more. This is the agenda for the Africa Prosperity Dialogues, taking place in Accra from 13–15 January 2027: “The Africa We Want Is Borderless. Move Freely. Pay Seamlessly. Trade More.” When Africans move, their money and businesses should move with them. For us at APN, free movement and seamless payments go hand in hand, and trusted digital identity can help connect the two. Join us to help make all this possible by registering at: www.apd2027.africaprosperitynetwork.com The author is the Founder and Executive Chairman of APN. He can be reached at gabby@africaprosperity.network .

items.title: 2027: Presidency seeks global safeguards against AI-generated falsehoods
items.description: –As Onanuga warns of threat to democratic institutions, public trust By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA–THE Presidency has called for urgent global action to check the growing misuse of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in political communication, warning that unchecked deployment of the technology could undermine democratic institutions, distort electoral processes and erode public trust ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Information and Strategy, Mr Bayo Onanuga, made the call on Thursday in Beijing, China, while delivering a paper titled, “AI and the Future of Global Communication”, at the 7th World Media Summit organised by Xinhua News Agency and the People’s Government of Beijing Municipality. Onanuga said the proliferation of AI-generated videos, images and other digital content for political purposes had made it imperative for governments, media organisations and technology stakeholders to establish safeguards against disinformation and manipulation. According to him, social media platforms, including X, Facebook and TikTok, were increasingly inundated with AI-generated content designed to advance political interests, entertain audiences and influence public opinion. With political activities and campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections gathering momentum, the presidential aide said AI had become a powerful instrument in the hands of politicians and their supporters, with the potential to serve both legitimate and destructive purposes. “We are in the thick of the political season and campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections, where new political leaders at the national and sub-national levels will be elected. AI, for good and bad, has become a powerful tool for electoral contests for politicians and their supporters. “Some political actors use AI to spread falsehoods, some use it satirically for entertainment, and some highlight candidates’ achievements,” he said. He stressed that the growing influence of AI in political communication demanded greater responsibility from political actors, media organisations and the general public, particularly in verifying information before creating, publishing or sharing digital content. While acknowledging the dangers associated with the technology, Onanuga cautioned against disregarding its enormous contributions to human development, particularly in medicine, mathematics and other areas of scientific innovation. He noted that AI had become deeply embedded in everyday life, citing its applications in vehicle safety systems, navigation and other technological solutions that had improved human efficiency and convenience. “Today, AI governs our existence, and we encounter it all the time. In the car, it warns you about your immediate surroundings. It maps your fastest route to your destination. We can go on, citing AI’s Leviathan impact on our lives. “I believe we can no longer ignore AI’s penetrating impact, most of it beneficial, unless we want to return to the Stone Age,” he added. The presidential aide expressed optimism that concerns over the growing influence of AI were receiving attention globally, with individuals, scientists and governments, including the United Nations, advocating appropriate measures to regulate its development and deployment. He, however, urged the international community to move swiftly beyond discussions and translate concerns into concrete safeguards, warning that failure to act could expose humanity to the harmful consequences of unchecked artificial intelligence. “The world must act before it becomes too late. Build guardrails quickly to save humanity,” he added. The post 2027: Presidency seeks global safeguards against AI-generated falsehoods appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Health experts push for nationwide newborn screening as Ghana marks 30 years of sickle cell detection
items.description: Health experts are calling for expanded newborn screening for sickle cell disease in Ghana, warning that more than half of affected children could die before the age of five if they are not diagnosed early and given appropriate care. This comes as Ghana marks 30 years of newborn screening for sickle cell disease, with experts raising concerns about limited access to testing and the country’s reliance on donor funding to sustain screening programmes. Head of Haematology at the Hospital for Sick Children and the University of Toronto’s Centre for Global Child Health, Professor Isaac Odame, said early diagnosis and simple medical interventions could save almost all babies born with the condition. He estimated that one in every 50 babies born in Ghana has sickle cell disease, making early detection critical to reducing preventable deaths. Speaking at an event to mark the 30th anniversary of newborn screening in Ghana, Prof. Odame stressed that screening must be expanded to reach more babies across the country. “One, we know that one in every 50 babies born in Ghana has sickle cell disease, and we do know that if you detect them early and you do simple interventions, almost all of them will survive to become adults,” he said. He warned that children who are not screened and diagnosed early face a significantly higher risk of dying before their fifth birthday. “If you don’t screen them or test them, more than half of them will die before the age of five years,” he cautioned. Prof. Odame described newborn screening as a life-saving intervention but expressed concern that only a few health facilities in Ghana currently offer the service. He also pointed to the funding challenges facing existing programmes, saying their operations depended heavily on support from donors. “This screening is a life-saving intervention, but as we speak in Ghana, only a few centres do the screening, and even where it is being done, it is dependent on donor funding,” he said. His comments have renewed calls for the government and health authorities to make newborn screening more widely available and ensure sustainable funding for early diagnosis and treatment. A haematology nurse specialist at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Diana Baidoo, also raised concerns about the number of babies testing positive for sickle cell disease through the hospital’s screening programme. She disclosed that about 1.8 per cent of babies tested so far had been found to have the condition, a figure she said was consistent with previous findings. “So far, we’ve estimated that 1.8 per cent of all the babies that we have tested have tested positive, and that is in line with what we’ve had,” she said. Although she could not provide the exact number of babies screened, she explained that the findings meant approximately two out of every 100 babies tested had the disease. “I’ll not be able to give you the actual numbers, but every two out of every 100 babies that we’ve tested have tested positive,” she added. The nurse specialist warned that delayed diagnosis could expose affected children to serious health complications, including stroke and infections, which could eventually lead to death. She said the importance of identifying babies with the condition early so they could receive the necessary medical attention before complications develop. “Complications, if the child is delayed in being identified as having the disease, they can have complications such as stroke, they can have infections, and ultimately they can die,” she said.

items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto A faction of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State, led by Alhaji Faruku Umar, has declared Hon. Zaki Muhammad Tambuwal the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 general election, challenging the emergence of Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya as the party’s candidate. The faction announced its position at a press conference on Thursday at the Press Centre in Sokoto, saying its decision followed a recent Federal High Court judgment in Abuja nullifying the emergence of former ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark. Umar, who described himself as the acclaimed chairman of the ADC in Sokoto State, said the faction had reaffirmed its loyalty to the leadership of Nafiu Bala following what it described as his court victory. He said the judgment had strengthened the faction’s resolve to uphold constitutionalism, internal democracy and the rule of law within the party. According to him, the faction considers Tambuwal the duly nominated and legitimate governorship candidate of the ADC in Sokoto State ahead of the 2027 elections. Umar said the declaration was intended to ensure that the party’s leadership and candidate-selection processes conformed with its constitution and democratic principles. He added that the faction would continue to recognise Bala’s leadership and work towards strengthening the party’s structures across the state. The faction also congratulated Bala on the court judgment, describing it as an important development in the ADC’s ongoing leadership dispute. Umar assured party supporters of the faction’s commitment to justice, internal democracy and constitutionalism, which he said were essential to the party’s progress and electoral prospects. He said the faction would mobilise its supporters behind Tambuwal as preparations for the 2027 governorship election gathered momentum. The declaration challenges the position of Dan’iya, who had previously been presented as the ADC’s governorship candidate in the state, and adds another dimension to the party’s leadership and candidate-selection dispute. Umar called on ADC supporters in Sokoto to remain united and committed to the party’s constitutional processes, insisting that the faction’s position was guided by the need to protect its democratic integrity. The press conference comes amid the broader leadership crisis within the ADC, which has continued to shape political alignments and internal contestations ahead of the 2027 elections. The faction maintained that its declaration of Tambuwal was consistent with its interpretation of the court judgment and the party’s constitutional provisions. It expressed confidence that the development would provide direction for the party in Sokoto State, while reaffirming its support for Bala’s leadership. The post Sokoto ADC faction declares Zaki Tambuwal 2027 candidate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ADC: Sokoto turnout prompted judgment voiding Atiku’s candidacy
items.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has alleged that the turnout at its political event in Sokoto influenced the timing of a court judgment that nullified the leadership of its David Mark-led faction and voided the party’s presidential candidacy. The party’s spokesperson, Bolaji Abdullahi, made the allegation on Channels Television’s Lunchtime Politics , while reacting to the judgment. Abdullahi said the party would challenge the ruling, insisting that the legal battle was part of what he described as sustained efforts to frustrate its political activities. He claimed that the ruling party was determined to remain in power and prevent Nigerians from having a democratic choice in the 2027 elections. “We’ve spent more time in the courts than we’ve spent on the campaign grounds, thanks to the ruling party,” he said. The ADC spokesperson alleged that the judgment was expedited following the party’s political outing in Sokoto. “But I think in the matter of hours after seeing what happened in Sokoto yesterday, the kind of reaction, the kind of turnout in Sokoto yesterday, they had to quickly go and dust up this and hurry up the judgment this morning,” Abdullahi said. He, however, said the ADC remained confident in its ability to challenge the ruling through the judicial process. “We will approach the same court. We believe in the judicial institution, regardless of the recklessness of some judges who have allowed themselves to be used as a tool for subverting democracy in Nigeria,” he said. Abdullahi said the party would apply for a stay of execution and appeal the judgment. He warned that if the ruling stood, the ADC could be prevented from fielding candidates for the presidential, governorship, National Assembly and other elections. “What is endangered is not the African Democratic Congress. What is endangered is Nigeria as a country and our democracy as we’ve known it,” he said. The ADC spokesperson maintained that the party’s message of change, affordability and improved living conditions had gained nationwide support, urging that Nigerians be allowed to choose their preferred leaders. He insisted that the judgment would not stand, adding that the party would continue its legal challenge. The post ADC: Sokoto turnout prompted judgment voiding Atiku’s candidacy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Orpailleurs venus de Guinée : Bamako face à l’afflux
items.description: © JDM Contraints de quitter plusieurs sites d’orpaillage de Siguiri, en Guinée, des milliers de ressortissants étrangers ont rejoint le Mali depuis le début de la semaine. À Bamako, leur arrivée mobilise les autorités maliennes et burkinabè pour organiser leur accueil et leur retour. « Nous sommes en famille au Mali, mais notre souhait est de rentrer chez nous », confie Yacouba Sawadogo, orpailleur burkinabè arrivé après avoir quitté la Guinée. Depuis le 29 octobre, les autorités guinéennes ont suspendu l’orpaillage artisanal dans la région de Siguiri, invoquant la dégradation de l’environnement, la pollution des cours d’eau et l’utilisation de machines incompatibles avec l’exploitation artisanale. Plusieurs sites ont fermé, poussant de nombreux étrangers au départ. Devant l’ambassade du Burkina Faso à Bamako, des centaines de personnes, dont des femmes et des adolescents, attendaient mercredi leur rapatriement. Yacouba Sawadogo affirme avoir quitté un site situé à une quinzaine de kilomètres de Siguiri après une opération menée sans préavis. Il évoque des machines détruites ou brûlées, des vols et des violences. Ces accusations n’ont pas été confirmées par les autorités guinéennes, qui assurent que les opérations visent l’orpaillage illégal et doivent respecter les droits humains. L’étudiant de l’Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo dit avoir travaillé dans l’orpaillage faute d’autres revenus. Selon lui, différentes contributions prélevées sur les sites réduisaient les gains des travailleurs. Son objectif est désormais de rejoindre le Burkina Faso et de retrouver sa famille. À Bamako, les besoins immédiats concernent l’alimentation, l’hébergement et le transport. Le passage par le Mali s’explique aussi par l’itinéraire terrestre et par le fait que l’ambassade burkinabè à Bamako couvre également la Guinée. Mobilisation Face à l’afflux, le Centre de coordination et de gestion des crises a tenu une réunion d’urgence et annoncé des dispositions pour accueillir les personnes concernées puis organiser leur acheminement vers leurs pays d’origine. Le Burkina Faso a, de son côté, dépêché une délégation ministérielle à Bamako. L’Amicale des travailleurs burkinabè au Mali a lancé un appel aux contributions. Selon son Président, Jean-Paul Ouattara, des cars ont été mobilisés. André Ouédraogo, membre de l’Association des ressortissants burkinabè au Mali, indiquait mercredi qu’une dizaine de bus avaient déjà quitté Bamako pour Ouagadougou. Siaka Ouattara, installé au Mali depuis cinq ans, appelle à une réponse plus large. « C’est une situation humanitaire qui doit être prise en charge comme toute autre », estime-t-il, souhaitant une mobilisation des organisations humanitaires et des États concernés. Joseph A. DEMBÉLÉ et Ali SANKARÉ

items.title: SDP rejects ‘Rainbow Coalition’, vows to contest 2027
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has declared that it will participate in the 2027 general elections, distancing itself from the proposed ‘Rainbow Coalition’ and insisting that it has no intention of entering any political arrangement that could compromise its identity. The party also accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of allegedly plotting to infiltrate opposition parties and weaken their ranks ahead of the elections. The National Chairman of the SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, stated these on Thursday in Abuja while addressing journalists after a marathon meeting with the party’s nine governorship candidates from different states. Gombe said the SDP had no interest in joining any arrangement that would compromise its political identity or align its candidates with the ruling party. He alleged that the APC, having lost public confidence over its governance record, was using the proposed coalition to woo opposition members and undermine the unity of other political parties. The chairman, however, said the SDP was working with other opposition parties towards building a coalition of Nigerians committed to credible elections, including joint training of party agents and the establishment of common situation rooms to protect votes at polling units. He reaffirmed the party’s commitment to presenting what he described as credible alternatives to Nigerians, particularly its presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and running mate, Prof. Usman Bugaje. Gombe said: “I want to assure you that SDP, as a political party, has nothing to do with anything called Rainbow Coalition. “We are with other political parties in the opposition, doing everything possible to rescue our dear country through a coalition of the Nigerian people. “We are not into any Rainbow Coalition where we will have candidates here and profess support for the APC presidency. We are SDP and we are for SDP candidates.” He said the party had also resolved to discipline any member who participated in the proposed arrangement without its authorisation. According to him, the meeting with the governorship candidates was part of preparations to strengthen the party’s electoral strategies and improve its chances in the 2027 general elections. He said the engagement provided an opportunity for candidates from different states to share experiences, identify organisational gaps and develop strategies for winning elections at national and state levels. Gombe urged Nigerians to assess the party’s candidates based on their competence, capacity, character and patriotism. He also pledged the SDP’s commitment to credible elections, saying it would collaborate with other opposition parties on election monitoring, training of polling agents and the establishment of joint situation rooms. “We will be our own INEC at the polling units and our own security to ensure free, fair and credible elections come 2027,” he said. The SDP chairman also raised concerns over the alleged failure of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish the names of some of the party’s candidates, saying the matter was already before the court. He accused the commission of failing to recognise the candidates despite what he described as the party’s compliance with the Electoral Act, the Constitution and its internal nomination procedures. Gombe also condemned what he described as attempts to disqualify the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, insisting that political parties should be allowed to freely present candidates for elections. He called on the judiciary, security agencies and INEC to remain impartial and protect the country’s democratic process. The chairman further expressed concerns over issues relating to the voters’ register and the creation of polling units, warning against actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process. Earlier, the Chairman of the SDP Governors’ Forum and Nasarawa State governorship candidate, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, said the meeting was aimed at developing strategies to secure victory in the presidential, governorship and legislative elections. Adamu said the candidates shared experiences from their respective states and discussed ways to address organisational gaps ahead of the polls. He expressed confidence that Nigerians were seeking an alternative to the APC-led government, adding that the SDP would prioritise citizens’ welfare and improved living conditions. The meeting brought together the party’s nine governorship candidates and members of its National Working Committee as part of efforts to strengthen its structures and preparations for the 2027 general elections. The governorship candidates were from Nasarawa, Oyo, Benue, Niger, Adamawa, Plateau, Kano, Gombe and Bauchi states The post SDP rejects ‘Rainbow Coalition’, vows to contest 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Les exportations hors hydrocarbures ont progressé de près de 1 milliard $ en 2025
items.description: Les exportations algériennes hors hydrocarbures ont fait un bond de près de 1 milliard de dollars en 2025 par rapport à 2024. Les chiffres ont été dévoilés ce jeudi 5 novembre par le ministre du Commerce extérieur et de la Promotion des exportations, Kamel Rezig. Selon le ministre, qui s’exprimait lors d’une séance de questions orales au Conseil de la nation, les exportations de l'Algérie en dehors du gaz et du pétrole ont atteint 5,16 milliards de dollars à la fin de l’année 2025, enregistrant une hausse de 972 millions de dollars par rapport à leur niveau de l’année 2024. En 2026, l’Algérie s’attend à 5 milliards de dollars d’exportations de produits hors pétrole et gaz. Dattes : 75 millions de dollars d'exportations durant le 1 er semestre 2026 Kamel Rezig a aussi fait état d’une “ évolution positive ” des exportations de dattes dans la période allant de 2024 jusqu'au premier semestre de l'année 2026. La valeur des exportations de ce produit s’est élevée en 2024 à un total de 78,06 millions de dollars, pour passer à 98,32 millions de dollars en 2025. Pendant le premier semestre de l’année en cours, les exportations de dattes ont généré 75,04 millions de dollars, a-t-il fait savoir. Fonds spécial des exportations : 3 900 dossiers déposés Kamel Rezig a mis en avant les axes de la stratégie nationale de développement des exportations, qui repose sur l'amélioration de l'infrastructure générale des exportations et la facilitation des activités des entreprises exportatrices, ainsi que sur l'élaboration de plans d’exportation spécifiques aux secteurs prioritaires, tout en accompagnant les entreprises exportatrices. Parmi les mécanismes pratiques mis en place pour accompagner les exportateurs, le ministre a cité le Fonds spécial de promotion des exportations. Ce fonds a enregistré, en 2025, un total de 3 900 dossiers déposés par des exportateurs afin de bénéficier principalement d’une prise en charge d’une partie des frais de participation aux manifestations économiques internationales et de transport international, a révélé M. Rezig. L’article Les exportations hors hydrocarbures ont progressé de près de 1 milliard $ en 2025 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Tchamba : Des acteurs sensibilisés sur le nouveau dispositif de prévention et de gestion des conflits fonciers et agropastoraux
items.description: Tchamba, 5 nov. (ATOP) – Un atelier préfectoral d’information et de sensibilisation des Services techniques déconcentrés (STD) et des leaders communautaires sur le nouveau dispositif de prévention et de gestion des conflits fonciers et agropastoraux s’est tenu les 4 et 5 novembre à Tchamba. La rencontre a été placée sous le thème : « Comprendre et s’approprier le nouvel arrêté préfectoral relatif à la gestion du pastoralisme dans la préfecture de Tchamba ». Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet « Redynamisation des valeurs endogènes et des innovations locales sur le climat et la souveraineté alimentaire » (REVEIL). Ce projet est piloté par l’Institut africain pour le développement économique et social (INADES-Formation Togo) en collaboration avec ses partenaires. L’atelier a pour objectif d’informer et de sensibiliser les autorités locales et les autres parties prenantes sur le nouvel arrêté et le dispositif de mise en place des comités cantonaux de prévention et de gestion des conflits fonciers et agropastoraux. Il a permis d’expliquer les raisons et les enjeux du changement de dispositif, de présenter les principales dispositions du nouvel arrêté, de clarifier les missions, attributions et le fonctionnement des nouveaux comités, ainsi que leur composition et les modalités de représentation des différentes catégories d’acteurs. La rencontre a également servi de cadre pour préciser les rôles des acteurs concernés et les étapes de mise en place des dix comités cantonaux. Les participants ont discuté du mécanisme de collaboration entre les comités cantonaux, les communes, les commissions domaniales, les chefferies et les services techniques. Le préfet de Tchamba, Issaka Laguebande, a indiqué que la préfecture est confrontée à des enjeux liés à la gestion du foncier rural, à la coexistence entre agriculteurs et éleveurs, à la transhumance et à l’accès partagé aux ressources naturelles, susceptibles d’engendrer des tensions et des conflits, nécessitant des mécanismes locaux de prévention et de gestion concertée. « Toutefois, les enseignements tirés de leur fonctionnement ont mis en évidence la nécessité de disposer de structures plus inclusives, légitimes, crédibles et fonctionnelles, adaptées aux réalités locales et mieux articulées avec les autorités administratives, les collectivités territoriales, les chefferies traditionnelles et les services techniques compétents », a-t-il expliqué. L’atelier a réuni les chefs canton, des propriétaires terriens, des éleveurs, des exploitants agricoles ainsi que les chefs de service déconcentrés de l’Etat concernés. Le maire de la commune Tchamba 3, Ebeh Yao, le 2 è adjoint au maire de la commune Tchamba 1, Latifou Oumorou et le représentant de INADES-Formation Togo, Akpotor Komi Lologno, y ont pris part. ATOP/SA/MEK/MD
