items.title: «Le grimoire de l’événementiel en Afrique de l’Ouest» : Mamadou Baïlo Danso veut transformer l’improvisation en industrie
items.description: Et si l’événementiel africain cessait d’être perçu comme une succession d’initiatives ponctuelles pour devenir une véritable industrie, structurée, professionnelle et compétitive ? C’est le pari audacieux que porte Mamadou Baïlo Danso dans son ouvrage Le grimoire de l’événementiel en Afrique de l’Ouest, édité par L’Harmattan Guinée. À travers ce livre, l’auteur pose un regard lucide sur un secteur en pleine mutation, mais encore confronté à de nombreux défis : manque de structuration, insuffisance de professionnalisation, faible anticipation, difficultés organisationnelles et recours encore fréquent à l’improvisation. Pour Danso, l’Afrique ne manque pourtant ni de talents, ni de créativité, ni d’événements. Elle doit surtout apprendre à transformer ces atouts en une véritable expertise. Quinze années de terrain pour une méthode Le « grimoire » est avant tout le fruit d’une longue expérience. Quinze années passées au contact du monde de l’événementiel, plus de 250 événements observés et l’écoute de quarante grandes figures du secteur nourrissent la réflexion de l’auteur. Loin de se limiter à un manuel technique, l’ouvrage ambitionne ainsi de proposer une véritable philosophie de l’événementiel. Sa particularité réside notamment dans les soixante lois que Mamadou Baïlo Danso met en avant pour aider les professionnels à repenser leurs pratiques. Derrière le choix du mot « grimoire », volontairement évocateur, se dessine l'idée d'un ouvrage qui rassemble des connaissances, des expériences et des principes destinés à devenir des outils de travail. Il s'agit, en quelque sorte, de transformer l'expérience accumulée sur le terrain en savoir transmissible. L’excellence ne se décrète pas, elle se prépare Pour le jeune auteur, la réussite d’un événement ne dépend pas uniquement des budgets disponibles ou de la reproduction de modèles venus d’ailleurs. Elle repose d’abord sur la discipline, la préparation, l’anticipation et la responsabilité. Cette approche donne au livre une dimension particulièrement intéressante dans le contexte africain. Car si les grands événements se multiplient sur le continent — festivals, concerts, salons, conférences, cérémonies, rencontres sportives ou culturelles — leur organisation demeure parfois marquée par des pratiques artisanales. Mamadou Baïlo Danso invite donc à changer de paradigme : ne plus considérer l’événementiel comme une activité accessoire, mais comme un secteur économique et culturel à part entière. Cette transformation passe par la formation des professionnels, la maîtrise des outils de communication, la connaissance des publics, la gestion des risques, la qualité de l'accueil, la maîtrise des délais et, surtout, la capacité à construire des expériences qui restent dans les mémoires. Quand les réalités africaines deviennent une force L’un des intérêts majeurs du grimoire de l’événementiel en Afrique de l’Ouest réside dans son ancrage. L’auteur ne propose pas simplement de copier les standards internationaux. Il cherche plutôt à montrer comment les réalités africaines, les héritages culturels et les savoir-faire locaux peuvent être intégrés aux exigences professionnelles contemporaines. Cette rencontre entre tradition et modernité, entre identité culturelle et standards internationaux, constitue l’une des clés de la vision défendue dans l’ouvrage. L’événementiel devient alors bien plus qu’une question de scène, de lumière, de sonorisation ou de protocole. Il devient un espace où se rencontrent culture, économie, communication, tourisme, créativité et identité. Un ouvrage pour ceux qui font et pensent l’événementiel Promoteurs, techniciens, entrepreneurs culturels, communicants, institutions, décideurs ou membres de la diaspora : le public auquel s’adresse l’ouvrage est large. Son ambition est de contribuer à faire émerger une nouvelle génération de professionnels capables de passer « du chaos à la maîtrise » et « de l’amateurisme à la construction » d’un véritable écosystème africain de l’événementiel. Cette ambition trouve un prolongement naturel dans le parcours de son auteur. Entrepreneur, stratège en communication, spécialiste du marketing digital et producteur d’événements culturels, Mamadou Baïlo Danso est également le fondateur de Dadia Communication. Installé au Canada, il évolue à la croisée de plusieurs univers et cherche à créer des passerelles professionnelles entre l’Afrique et l’Amérique du Nord. Un plaidoyer pour une industrie culturelle souveraine Au-delà des techniques et des conseils pratiques, Le grimoire de l’événementiel en Afrique de l’Ouest apparaît finalement comme un plaidoyer. Celui d’un secteur africain qui entend prendre confiance en ses propres capacités. Car l’enjeu dépasse la seule réussite d’un concert, d’un festival ou d’une conférence. Professionnaliser l’événementiel, c’est aussi créer des emplois, valoriser les talents, stimuler les industries culturelles et créatives, attirer des investissements et renforcer l’attractivité des territoires. Avec cet ouvrage de 9 chapitres pour 200 pages, édité par L’Harmattan Guinée, Mamadou Baïlo Danso ouvre donc un débat essentiel : comment faire de l’immense créativité africaine une véritable force économique, culturelle et professionnelle ? Le grimoire apporte ses propres clés. Aux acteurs du secteur désormais de s’en emparer pour écrire les prochaines pages de l’événementiel africain.

Official says 273 arrested in NCCIA raid on 'illegal' call centre on Karachi's Sharea Faisal
items.description: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Thursday claimed to have conducted a major operation against an alleged international fraud network and arrested 273 people from a call centre located on Sharea Faisal. Addressing a press conference in Karachi, NCCIA Additional Director, Shahzad Akbar, said 339 laptops, 152 cell phones and four computers were seized during the operation. “The NCCIA conducted a major enforcement operation on Nov 4 at a premises located near Kavish Crown Plaza in connection with an ongoing enquiry into an alleged international financial fraud network and call centre,” he said. During the operation, the investigating team identified a call centre operating under the name Voxtron Solutions. According to preliminary findings, it was allegedly involved in fraudulent activities targeting foreign nationals through impersonation, identity misuse and caller ID spoofing, he said. According to Akbar, initial investigations indicated that the facility was allegedly operating under the pretext of providing debt validation services. “Personnel associated with the operation reportedly impersonated representatives of foreign banking institutions and debt validation service providers, contacting individuals abroad and offering assistance in the verification and validation of their outstanding financial obligations,” he stated. The NCCIA official said investigators had established “reasonable grounds” to suspect that the alleged scheme was designed to induce victims into disclosing sensitive personal and financial information, including Social Security Numbers and payment card credentials. He said preliminary findings further suggested that the information obtained was subsequently exploited to facilitate unauthorised financial transactions through merchant accounts. The proceeds generated through these transactions were reportedly transferred to Pakistan through company accounts and remittance channels, indicating possible cross-border movement of illicit funds, he said. Akbar said all recovered evidence and material was taken into official custody and referred for detailed technical examination and digital forensic analysis. Akbar said 273 suspects were arrested for further investigation and proceedings and a case was registered under Sections 3 (unauthorised access to information system or data), 4 (unauthorised copying or transmission of data), 13 (electronic forgery), 14 (electronic fraud), 16 (unauthorised use of identity information) and 26 (spoofing) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (Peca). Families stage protest Meanwhile, the suspects’ relatives and local residents staged a protest against the raid and arrests near the Baloch Colony Bridge on Sharea Faisal, disrupting the smooth flow of traffic along Karachi’s main artery. The demonstrators protested the arrest of around 100 women from the call centre, claiming that their children worked there and had no involvement in illegal activities, demanding the suspects’ immediate release. A traffic police spokesperson said that because of the protest, traffic was diverted on alternative routes. Local police and traffic officials held talks with the protesters and persuaded them to disperse. Traffic flow was restored on the main road by 1:22pm. Last week, the agency claimed to have arrested over 40 suspects during a raid on an “illegal call centre” located on Sharea Faisal. An NCCIA spokesperson alleged that the call centre was involved in fraud against foreigners.

items.title: Égypte : Hossam Hassan vers la sortie, plusieurs pistes pour lui succéder
items.description: La Fédération égyptienne de football aurait décidé de mettre fin aux fonctions de Hossam Hassan à la tête de la sélection nationale. Selon Al-Masry Al-Youm, le technicien et son frère Ibrahim Hassan devraient quitter leurs fonctions à l’issue des deux prochains matchs de l’Égypte face au Malawi, prévus dans le cadre des qualifications à la CAN 2027. D’après une source citée par le média égyptien, les deux rencontres contre le Malawi constitueraient les dernières du staff actuel. La décision serait liée à plusieurs tensions et difficultés apparues au cours des derniers mois. Suspendu pour trois matchs, Hossam Hassan ne devrait pas diriger l’équipe depuis le banc lors de ces deux rendez-vous. C’est Tarek Soliman qui assurerait la direction technique depuis le terrain. La principale surprise concerne le profil envisagé pour succéder à Hossam Hassan. La Fédération privilégierait actuellement la piste d’un entraîneur égyptien. Parmi les noms évoqués figurent Hossam El-Badry et Ali Maher. Le choix n’est toutefois pas encore définitif. Certaines voix au sein de la Fédération plaideraient également pour la nomination d’un technicien étranger. Le dossier devrait être tranché après les deux matchs contre le Malawi. La décision officielle pourrait intervenir dans les prochaines heures, après consultation de Chawki Gharib, selon le média égyptien. Certains responsables auraient également proposé de repousser l’annonce après la trêve internationale de novembre afin de ne pas perturber la préparation de la sélection. L’Égypte doit affronter le Malawi à deux reprises dans le cadre des troisième et quatrième journées des qualifications pour la CAN 2027. items.title: JUSAG cites pay disparities, working conditions in defence of strike
items.description: The General Secretary of the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG), Abdulai Yakubu, has cited disparities between judicial workers’ legal entitlements and their actual take-home pay, alongside the strict professional standards they are required to uphold, as reasons for the association’s ongoing strike. According to him, the Judicial Service employees are held to high standards of integrity and professionalism but are not adequately remunerated in line with the conditions they are expected to work under. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Thursday, November 5, Mr Yakubu said the financial difficulties confronting some workers have become so severe that a number of them struggle to meet basic needs, including transportation to and from work. He recounted instances where workers have told him they cannot return home after closing because they cannot afford transport. “Sometimes you close, you meet people, what time are you closing? I’m not going home. I can’t go home. General, I can’t go home. I said why? I can’t afford transport to go home,” he said. Mr Yakubu stressed that the issue goes beyond the salaries workers receive, pointing to what he described as a significant gap between their legally established entitlements and actual take-home pay. He cited an example of an employee entitled to GH¢3,000 but receiving about GH¢1,500 as take-home pay. “I can tell you that somebody who is entitled to, let’s say, 3,000 Ghana cedis is paid, let’s say, around 1,500. And that will be a take-home salary. Somebody entitled to 1,500. Negotiated for 3,000, you are paying 1,500,” he said. He questioned why judicial workers should have to negotiate for benefits and remuneration that are already provided for by law. “The law provides for 3,000 cedis, and you are paid 1,500. Why do we have to negotiate when it comes to application of law?” he asked. The JUSAG General Secretary also drew attention to the strict ethical and professional requirements imposed on judicial service employees. He said workers are prohibited from accepting gifts from individuals, with such conduct potentially attracting serious disciplinary action, including dismissal. They are also barred from engaging in partisan politics and are required to adhere to a prescribed dress code. He said that these expectations should be matched by remuneration that reflects the standards and responsibilities of the work they perform. “And we’re saying that once we are subjected to this high-level standard of integrity in the work we do, then pay us by the standards that we are supposed to work with,” he said. Mr Yakubu further questioned why judicial service employees appear to face difficulties in securing their entitlements compared with workers in other public institutions. He cited employees of the Parliamentary Service, saying their salaries are regulated by law and paid in accordance with the provisions. He also questioned why employees of the Office of the President do not appear to face similar challenges in securing their remuneration. “Why does it have to be judicial service staff, employees serving the third arm of government?” he asked.

items.title: Ghana’s BRICS partnership proposal came from Akufo-Addo-era committee – Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama says Ghana’s decision to pursue a partnership with the BRICS bloc was first recommended by a ministerial committee set up under the previous administration led by Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo. He disclosed this at a meet-the-press session at Jubilee House on Thursday, November 5, 2026, explaining that the proposal was already before Cabinet when he assumed office and was later approved by his government. According to him, his administration did not initiate the process but inherited the recommendation and subjected it to Cabinet consideration before endorsing the proposed partnership. “Let me also tell you, the ministerial committee that sat and recommended that Ghana should accede to BRICS partnership was under Nana Akufo-Addo,” he said. Mr Mahama further explained: “We came and met their recommendation. And so, we didn’t set up the ministerial committee. It was set up under the former NPP administration.” He said Cabinet subsequently assessed the proposal and agreed that Ghana’s participation as a BRICS partner would be beneficial. “And so, the recommendation was submitted to Cabinet. And so, when we came, we met it. And so, Cabinet sat on it and said, it’s a good idea to be a BRICS partner. And so, we approved it,” he added. The President also rejected suggestions that the partnership represents a departure from Ghana’s foreign policy tradition, insisting that closer engagement with the bloc is consistent with the country’s longstanding non-aligned position. BRICS comprises Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.

items.title: Bawumia urges government to prioritise gold reserves over trading
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has called on the government to focus on building Ghana’s gold reserves rather than trading in the commodity, arguing that the Bank of Ghana’s decision to trade part of its gold holdings resulted in losses of GH¢1.7 billion. He said the losses could have been avoided if the Gold for Reserves programme had been implemented with a focus on accumulating gold to strengthen the country’s reserves. At the town hall meeting in Tokyo, Japan, Dr Bawumia maintained that the programme should be geared towards building the country’s gold reserves rather than trading in the commodity. “If they had followed the way that we had wanted to do the Gold for Reserves programme in terms of accumulating reserves, those losses would not have been made. But once you decide to start trading in gold, you will make those losses,” he said. Dr Bawumia also defended his campaign focus on digitalisation ahead of the 2024 general elections, dismissing claims that he had steered clear of economic issues during the electioneering period. He explained that his focus on the sector was informed by the growing importance of technology in the global economy and the need for countries to establish the digital infrastructure required to compete. He emphasised the importance of digital infrastructure to economic growth, warning that countries that fail to adapt to the changing global economy risk losing out on opportunities. “Many people don’t understand that the world economy is now digital. The world economy is digital. If you don’t go digital, you cannot prosper in this global economy. You cannot. And if you don’t take your time and put your digital framework together, you’ll be left behind,” he said.

items.title: South Africans now leading drug trafficking cartels in Nigeria — NDLEA
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has raised the alarm over the growing involvement of South African nationals in drug trafficking networks operating in Nigeria, alleging that some are facilitating the movement of illicit substances through the country to other parts of the world. The agency said three South African nationals had been arrested in recent weeks with large consignments of heroin, cocaine and synthetic cannabis, popularly known as Loud. The Assistant Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Francis Okogun, disclosed this on Thursday during a joint media briefing by defence, security and intelligence agencies at the Office of the National Security Adviser in Abuja. Okogun said the arrests were significant because of the quantities of illicit drugs recovered and the potential implications for Nigeria’s international reputation. He said: “On the arrest of South African nationals in connection with drug trafficking, it is important to clarify that the issue has attracted attention because of the negative impression it could create about Nigeria internationally. “Our findings indicate that some foreign nationals are increasingly becoming involved in facilitating the movement of illicit drugs through Nigeria to other parts of the world. Some are also involved in bringing such substances into the country. “For the period under review, three individuals were arrested. What makes these arrests particularly significant is the large quantities of drugs recovered, including heroin, cocaine and synthetic cannabis, popularly known as Loud.” He said the agency was conducting investigations to establish the intended destinations of the seized drugs and identify the networks behind the consignments. “As you know, drug traffickers rarely volunteer information about their sponsors or the final destinations of their consignments. “We are therefore conducting painstaking investigations to establish the actual destinations of the drugs and identify the cartels responsible for the shipments,” he said. One of the recent arrests involved a 38-year-old South African woman, identified as Ms Will Jessica Ann, who was apprehended by NDLEA operatives at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after 5.75 kilogrammes of heroin were allegedly discovered in her luggage. The agency said the suspect concealed the drugs in 14 large blocks and allegedly used her three-year-old son as a cover to evade thorough security screening. She was arrested during the inward clearance of passengers aboard Qatar Airways flight QR 1433 from Doha to Abuja. According to the NDLEA, the suspect initially denied travelling with checked-in luggage but later admitted ownership of two bags after operatives established that their tags matched the claim tags attached to her passport. The agency said she claimed she had forgotten that she checked in the two bags. In another case in October 2026, a South African woman, Gebashe Sithandiwe Jessie, was arrested at the Port Harcourt International Airport for allegedly attempting to smuggle 32.74 kilogrammes of Thai Loud, a synthetic cannabis product, concealed in her luggage. The NDLEA said investigations were ongoing to uncover the wider trafficking networks and identify other individuals connected to the shipments. The post South Africans now leading drug trafficking cartels in Nigeria — NDLEA appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Prison illégale découverte en Ukraine : Zakharova dénonce les milliards de l'Occident pour des lieux de torture
items.description: Les lieux de torture, semblables a celui decouvert pres de Kiev , constituent le « pilier » du pouvoir de Volodymyr Zelensky, a declare le 5 novembre Maria Zakharova, la porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres. Selon elle, les Ukrainiens mobilises, retenus dans des sous-sols, ont servi de « materiel physiologique » pour « l'entraînement aux pratiques sadiques et banderistes du commandement », ainsi que de « sacs de frappe pour leurs surveillants ». « Il [Zelensky] ne se maintient que grâce a ces salles de torture, a la peur qu'elles sement dans la societe, a cette hostilite absolument folle entre les gens et a la haine qu'ils se vouent les uns aux autres. C'est dans ce climat que s'exerce son pouvoir. Et les piliers de ce pouvoir, ce sont precisement ces salles de torture. Cela englobe les centres territoriaux de recrutement, la "busification" [l'embarquement force dans des vehicules a des fins de mobilisation], la mobilisation ukrainienne, mais aussi l'arbitraire le plus total qui regne dans les rues des villes, des villages, des localites et des bourgades d'Ukraine », a-t-elle affirme. Maria Zakharova a egalement accuse les medias occidentaux de deformer les faits, soulignant que la BBC qualifie de « rumeurs » le passage a tabac d'Oleksy Pekour , un garcon de 14 ans evacue d'une prison clandestine, et qualifie de « propagande russe » la video des lieux. Elle a par ailleurs ajoute que la mise au jour de tels lieux de torture revele a quoi servent les milliards fournis par l'Occident. Une medecin et son chauffeur, arrives sur les lieux, arretes sans possibilite de liberation sous caution Le scandale qui a eclate en Ukraine apres la decouverte d'un centre de torture pres de Kiev prend une nouvelle tournure. Selon les medias, la police nationale et le Service de securite ukrainien ont lance une veritable chasse a l'homme contre ceux qui manifestaient devant le bâtiment et exigeaient la liberation des otages. Ainsi, les forces de l'ordre ukrainiennes ont identifie 130 participants presumes a la manifestation, ceux qui s'etaient rassembles devant le centre de torture illegal et posaient des questions genantes au chef de cabinet de Volodymyr Zelensky Kyrylo Boudanov, arrive en urgence sur place pour tenter d'apaiser la situation. Sur les reseaux sociaux de la police ukrainienne, des videos montrant les interpellations sont publiees, qualifiant les tentatives des manifestants de liberer les otages d'« emeutes ». L'une des victimes de la soi-disant justice ukrainienne est une femme, arrivee la premiere sur les lieux a bord d'une ambulance. Il s'agit de Valentina Moloda, une medecin qui a diffuse l'information concernant ce lieu de torture sur les reseaux sociaux. Lors de l'audience, elle a raconte que le 2 novembre, une habitante du quartier, Tatiana Kireïeva, lui avait ecrit que son mari, qui venait de subir une operation durant laquelle « on lui avait retire la stomie, c'est-a-dire la partie de l'intestin qui sortait par le ventre », etait detenu dans le sous-sol de cette maison. Moloda s'est ensuite rendue devant le bâtiment en question et a somme les militaires qui s'y trouvaient de liberer l'homme, mais ceux-ci ont refuse, ce qui a entraîne un conflit. Kyrylo Boudanov et le Service de securite ukrainien ont affirme que Moloda n'etait pretendument pas medecin et qu'elle avait provoque des affrontements a proximite d'un « poste de deploiement temporaire » de la Garde nationale ukrainienne en echange d'une remuneration. Cependant, a l'audience, Moloda a refute les accusations. Elle a presente des documents confirmant qu'elle est proprietaire de la clinique d'urgence Prime, ou elle est aussi medecin-chef. Le tribunal a place la femme en detention provisoire pour 60 jours sans possibilite de liberation sous caution. Toujours selon les medias ukrainiens, la prevenue est accusee d'entrave a l'action des forces armees ukrainiennes, de diffusion d'informations sur le deploiement des unites militaires et d'organisation de troubles a l'ordre public. La veille, elle avait ete ajoutee a la base de donnees du site ukrainien Mirotvorets, qui recense tous les « ennemis de l'Ukraine » depuis plus de 10 ans. Outre Moloda, le tribunal a rendu une decision similaire a l'encontre du conducteur de l'ambulance qui s'etait rendu avec Moloda a la prison illegale. Des dizaines d'otages, dont un garcon de 14 ans, dans une prison clandestine liee a Azov Les faits remontent au 2 novembre, lorsque des informations ont commence a circuler dans les medias ukrainiens et sur les reseaux sociaux au sujet d'un « site militaire secret » dans lequel seraient detenus et tortures des Ukrainiens mobilises de force et des deserteurs des forces armees ukrainiennes. Le site a ete place sous la responsabilite du 1er corps de la Garde nationale, lie a l'organisation terroriste Azov. L'affaire a eu un large retentissement et, des le soir meme, une foule s'est rassemblee devant la maison pour manifester et exiger la liberation des personnes detenues. Une quarantaine de personnes ont ete trouvees dans le sous-sol de la maison privee, certaines presentant des blessures graves et des signes pouvant indiquer des actes de torture. Le dossier a pris de l'ampleur apres la decouverte dans le bâtiment d'un mineur, Oleksy Pekour. Il a raconte qu'il avait ete traîne dans une maison et frappe a coups de pelle par des individus portant des cagoules. Lui et ses parents ont par la suite ete inscrits sur la meme liste Mirotvorets. Le depute ukrainien Artiom Dmitrouk a quant a lui declare que, dans cette maison, plusieurs personnes avaient ete battues a mort, puis declarees disparues. Pour sa part, un soldat ukrainien a indique que ces etablissements, surnommes « fosses », seraient utilises pour detenir des soldats accuses d'indiscipline ou de desertion, ou ils pourraient etre victimes de coups et d'humiliations. L'armee et la police sont arrivees devant la maison. Un sentiment d'indignation s'est rapidement propage parmi les habitants, ce qui a fini par degenerer en heurts avec les forces de l'ordre. La police a utilise des gaz lacrymogenes, les manifestants ont tente de renverser un bus et ont detruit une partie du mur. Des coups de feu ont ete signales, certains temoins accusant les forces de securite d'avoir ouvert le feu. Une personne a ete blessee a la tete.

DHQ denies ceasefire with Boko Haram, ISWAP, others
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Defence Headquarters has dismissed reports alleging that the Federal Government or the Nigerian military entered into a ceasefire agreement with Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) or any other terrorist group. The military said its sustained and intensified offensives against terrorists, armed bandits, kidnappers and other criminal groups demonstrated that no such agreement existed. In one of the reports, a media platform had claimed that the Federal Government entered into a secret ceasefire agreement with the Boko Haram faction led by Bakura Doro, which allegedly contributed to relative calm in parts of the North-East for about three months. The report, citing three individuals said to have contacts among senior Boko Haram members, claimed that the ceasefire had been in effect since June and was expected to be extended. However, the Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba, dismissed the allegation, saying ongoing military operations and the successes recorded against armed groups showed that troops were not relenting. “I want to make it clear that there is nothing like a ceasefire anywhere, with Boko Haram, ISWAP or any terrorist group. “Considering the terrorists neutralised, suspects arrested, victims rescued and other successes recorded across our operations, it is clear that we are not relenting. We will continue to sustain pressure on these criminal elements. “Our operations are not limited to Boko Haram or ISWAP. They also target kidnappers and other criminal elements who take up arms against innocent citizens,” he said. Uba warned that individuals involved in criminal activities threatening the lives and security of Nigerians would either be neutralised through lawful military operations or brought to justice. “Anyone involved in criminal activities that threaten the lives and security of Nigerians will either be eliminated through lawful military operations or brought to justice,” he said. On reports of terrorists and bandits moving into parts of the country where they were previously less active, the defence spokesman described the development as evidence of the impact of ongoing military operations but said the Armed Forces were not taking the situation lightly. “The fact that some of them are leaving their former locations is a testimony to the successes of our operations. However, I assure you that we are not taking the situation lightly,” he said. He explained that the military was mapping locations where the fleeing armed groups might have relocated and taking proactive measures to prevent them from establishing new footholds. Uba said recent adjustments to the Armed Forces’ order of battle, including the establishment of new formations, battalions and units, were aimed at closing security gaps and strengthening military presence in vulnerable areas. He added that the expansion of the military’s operational capacity and reach would help security forces contain the movement of terrorists and prevent them from extending their activities to other parts of the country. Giving an account of military operations over the last three months, Uba said troops conducted 588 distinct security operations in September and October. He disclosed that the operations resulted in the neutralisation of 435 terrorists and bandits, including high-profile commanders identified as Ali Mandara, Abba Gajiri, Habu Ikkima, Nakif Yana Faruk, Commander Gogore and Abdussamad Ohida. According to him, troops also arrested 809 suspects, secured the voluntary surrender of 198 insurgents and rescued 717 kidnapped victims and captives. Among those rescued, he listed 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Owerri, Imo State, and 11 persons in Danko-Wasagu, Kebbi State. The defence spokesman further disclosed that troops recorded major tactical successes against terrorists in Buni Yadi, Baga, Kukawa, Bittai and the Owo Forest. items.title: Près de 3 MMDH consacrés aux indemnités des imams en 2026
items.description: Le ministère des Habous et des Affaires islamiques a mobilisé une enveloppe de 2,94 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) en 2026 pour verser les indemnités de plus de 77.000 imams, muezzins et autres préposés religieux. Présentant le budget sectoriel devant la Chambre des représentants, Ahmed Taoufiq a également fait état de la poursuite des programmes de formation, du renforcement de la couverture sociale et de la construction de nouvelles mosquées, dont 198 réalisées à l’initiative de bienfaiteurs. Près de 3 MMDH sont consacrés cette année à la rémunération des personnels religieux au Maroc. Le ministre des Habous et des Affaires islamiques, Ahmed Taoufiq, a annoncé que son département avait réservé une enveloppe de 2,94 3 MMDH au versement des indemnités de plus de 77.000 imams, muezzins et autres préposés religieux au titre de l’exercice 2026. Cette annonce a été faite lors de la présentation du projet de budget sectoriel du ministère devant la Commission des affaires étrangères, de la défense nationale, des affaires islamiques et des Marocains résidant à l’étranger à la Chambre des représentants. Le ministre a également indiqué que la dernière tranche de l’augmentation de 300 dirhams des indemnités des imams et des muezzins avait été entièrement mise en œuvre, conformément aux hautes orientations royales. L’intervention d’Ahmed Taoufiq a permis de dresser un état des lieux des actions engagées par le ministère en matière d’encadrement religieux, de formation des personnels et d’amélioration de leurs conditions professionnelles et sociales. Formation et encadrement : près de 48.000 imams concernés Sur le volet de la formation, le ministre a indiqué que près de 48.000 imams avaient bénéficié du programme de mise à niveau relevant du dispositif « Mithaq Al Oulama », sous la supervision de 1.427 oulémas. Une enveloppe de 109,5 millions de dirhams a été mobilisée pour mettre en place les moyens et les outils nécessaires à ce programme. Le département poursuit également, en coordination avec le secrétariat général du Conseil supérieur des oulémas, un programme triennal de formation et de formation continue destiné aux imams et aux prédicateurs. Dans le cadre du projet « Waai Al Qorb », des formations ont été programmées au profit de près de 3.900 imams et mourchidates, ainsi que de 2.400 muezzins. © Mounir Mehimdate Le ministère a par ailleurs intégré des modules consacrés à l’intelligence artificielle et à la communication numérique. Ces formations ont bénéficié à 150 imams et mourchidates, dans l’objectif de renforcer leurs compétences face aux nouveaux outils de communication. Sur le plan professionnel, quelque 1.400 préposés religieux ont été mis à niveau et affectés à des fonctions, pour un budget annuel avoisinant les 20 millions de dirhams. Le ministère a aussi procédé au recrutement de 150 imams mourchidines et de 100 mourchidates, diplômés de l’Institut Mohammed VI de formation des imams, des mourchidines et des mourchidates, après une année de formation intensive. Plus de 272 millions de dirhams pour la couverture médicale L’amélioration des conditions sociales des personnels religieux constitue un autre volet important du programme présenté par le ministre. Ahmed Taoufiq a annoncé qu’une enveloppe dépassant 272 millions de dirhams avait été consacrée à la couverture médicale des préposés religieux et de leurs ayants droit. Les actions sociales comprennent également la prise en charge du pèlerinage au profit de 128 imams et muezzins, ainsi que de 36 personnes chargées de l’enseignement et de la mémorisation du Coran. De son côté, la Fondation Mohammed VI pour la promotion des œuvres sociales des préposés religieux a mobilisé 150 millions de dirhams en 2026 pour financer ses différents programmes au profit des personnels religieux, de leurs familles et des veuves. Ces interventions couvrent notamment les aides directes, les prestations sociales, les soins médicaux ainsi que les activités culturelles et sociales. Les campagnes médicales organisées par le ministère, dans une démarche de dépistage et de prévention des maladies, ont également permis à quelque 5.500 préposés religieux de bénéficier de consultations et d'examens. Plus de 23.000 mosquées couvertes par les programmes d'encadrement En matière d'encadrement religieux, le ministère poursuit, en coordination avec le secrétariat général du Conseil supérieur des oulémas, la mise en œuvre du plan « Al Tasdid wa Al Tabligh ». Une enveloppe de 23 millions de dirhams a été réservée aux moyens logistiques, techniques et administratifs nécessaires à son déploiement. Selon le ministre, le nombre de zones couvertes par ce dispositif a été élargi pour concerner désormais plus de 23.000 mosquées, encadrées par 400 imams et mourchidates. Le programme de prédication et d'orientation religieuse mobilise, pour sa part, près de 2.800 prédicateurs et 780 prédicatrices, sous la supervision des conseils scientifiques locaux dans les différentes régions du Royaume. Une enveloppe de 235 millions de dirhams a été allouée au secrétariat général du Conseil supérieur des oulémas ainsi qu'aux conseils scientifiques régionaux et locaux pour l'exercice 2026. © Mounir Mehimdate 198 mosquées construites à l'initiative de bienfaiteurs Le développement et la réhabilitation des lieux de culte figurent également parmi les priorités présentées par Ahmed Taoufiq. Le ministre a annoncé que les travaux de construction ou de reconstruction de 43 mosquées devraient être achevés d'ici la fin de l'année, pour un coût global de 227 millions de dirhams. Le lancement des travaux de construction ou de reconstruction de 36 autres mosquées est également prévu, avec un investissement de 237 millions de dirhams. Le ministre a par ailleurs fait état de la construction de 198 mosquées à l'initiative de bienfaiteurs, dont 68% se trouvent en milieu rural. Dans le cadre du programme national de réhabilitation des mosquées endommagées, 16 lieux de culte fermés doivent également être remis en état avant la fin de l'année, pour un montant avoisinant les 19 millions de dirhams. Le département a réservé 25 millions de dirhams à l'entretien des mosquées et de leurs équipements. Il a aussi programmé la restauration et l'aménagement de 100 mosquées, pour un coût de 68 millions de dirhams, tandis que les travaux de restauration de 99 mosquées historiques de Marrakech doivent être engagés, avec une enveloppe de 36 millions de dirhams. Au total, 120 millions de dirhams ont été mobilisés pour la restauration et l'équipement des mosquées, l'amélioration de l'éclairage, du chauffage et de la climatisation, ainsi que l'installation d'équipements facilitant les services aux fidèles et renforçant les conditions de sécurité. À Marrakech, un programme spécifique prévoit notamment l'équipement de 1.250 mosquées en chauffe-eau fonctionnant à l'énergie solaire, pour un budget de 25 millions de dirhams. Une initiative qui s'inscrit dans les efforts annoncés par le ministère en matière d'efficacité énergétique et de recours aux énergies renouvelables dans les lieux de culte. items.title: Hong Kong: Joshua Wong Gets Nearly 10 More Years in Prison
items.description: Click to expand Image Joshua Wong speaks to protesters near the Legislative Council in Hong Kong, June 17, 2019. © 2019 Kin Cheung/AP Photo (Tokyo) – The Hong Kong High Court on November 5, 2026, sentenced Joshua Wong, a well-known democracy activist, to 10 years in prison on baseless national security charges, Human Rights Watch said today. Two months of the sentence will run concurrently with his current national security sentence. Wong has been in custody since November 2020, when he was 24, and faces imprisonment until late 2036, when he will be 40. The Hong Kong government should immediately and unconditionally release Wong. Foreign governments should denounce the sentences against him and other wrongfully detained pro-democracy activists and impose targeted sanctions on officials responsible for Hong Kong’s growing repression. “The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars.” To keep Hong Kong society subdued, and to reduce the chance of an international outcry, the Hong Kong government appears to have adopted the tactic of stacking charges against influential pro-democracy leaders to ensure their prolonged detention, Human Rights Watch said. Other notable Hong Kong figures who have faced similar tactics include Jimmy Lai, founder of Apple Daily, and veteran democracy activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Albert Ho. The court sentenced Wong, 30, under the National Security Law for “conspiring to collude with foreign forces.” The authorities accused him of “conspiring” with the activist Nathan Law and other “unknown” individuals between 2016 and November 2020 to urge foreign governments to sanction Hong Kong and Chinese government officials as they advocated for Hong Kong’s “democratic self-determination.” The prosecution relied heavily on the international lobbying and media advocacy that Wong and Demosisto, the political party Wong co-founded in 2016, carried out before the National Security Law took effect. Wong initiated online petitions, spoke to international media, and met with foreign officials to draw attention to human rights abuses in Hong Kong. He urged governments to sanction Chinese and Hong Kong officials responsible for abuses and to stop selling weapons to Hong Kong police that they use to carry out rights violations. Wong had mostly stopped these activities before the National Security Law became effective. Demosisto disbanded on June 30, 2020, and Wong resigned from the group. However, the government quoted social media posts by Wong as ostensible evidence that his alleged “conspiracy” with Law to commit “foreign collusion” continued after the law took effect. In these posts, Wong said he “would not change his views” and that he would “continue to seek support from the international community” in his personal capacity, while Law and others abroad would continue their international advocacy. The government also cited Wong’s subsequent opinion pieces and media interviews, though none directly called for sanctions, which the National Security Law specifically prohibits. It also cited his reposts of Law’s posts broadly calling for sanctions against Chinese officials and Hong Kong police. The court ruled that Wong’s offense was of a “grave nature.” The National Security Law sets prison terms of 3 to 10 years for “foreign collusion,” or 10 years to life for offenses deemed to be of a “grave nature.” Wong formally pleaded guilty on September 2. A guilty plea normally results in a one-third sentence reduction. But a sentence reduction cannot bring the term below the statutory minimum. Because of reporting restrictions on pretrial committal proceedings, when a magistrate determines whether to send a case to a higher court for trial, the public did not know the details of the accusations against Wong until the formal plea. The government enacted a law in 2024 to enable the court, on national security grounds, to deny the defendant’s right to ask the court to lift restrictions on reporting about the case. By restricting media reporting on the pretrial proceedings in national security cases, the government can control the narrative and undermine the fundamental legal principle of open justice. Since Beijing imposed the National Security Law on Hong Kong in June 2020, Hong Kong authorities have used the new legal regime—along with existing laws—to rapidly dismantle civil society and detain, imprison, or force into exile hundreds of activists and government critics. Wong has been in custody since November 2020, when he pleaded guilty to two charges of organizing and inciting an unauthorized assembly linked to the 2019 citywide protest movement. After that, he pleaded guilty to five more charges on separate occasions, including for violating an anti-mask law, participating in an unauthorized vigil for the 1989 Tiananmen Massacre, and breaching a court ban to disclose a police officer’s personal information. While serving these sentences, Wong was charged with two national security offenses, which carry far harsher penalties. In January 2021, Wong was charged with “conspiring to commit subversion” for participating in an unofficial democratic primary in 2020 and sentenced to another four years and eight months in prison. Before Wong could complete these sentences, the authorities brought the “foreign collusion” charge against him in June 2025, ensuring that he would remain in prison. Wong became one of Hong Kong’s best-known democracy activists as a teenager, after leading a massive 2012 protest against a government educational curriculum widely seen as political indoctrination. He became the global face of Hong Kong’s democracy movement during the 2014 Umbrella Movement and co-founded Demosisto with Law and others in 2016. The party disbanded on June 30, 2020, hours before the National Security Law came into effect. The National Security Law’s sweeping provisions have been used to punish peaceful protest and expression. Its use against Wong and others violates the right to freedom of expression under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which is incorporated into Hong Kong law through the city’s de facto constitution, the Basic Law, and the Bill of Rights Ordinance. “Beijing has paid no real price for its increasing repression in Hong Kong,” Pearson said. “Concerned governments should press for the release of Wong and other activists, impose targeted sanctions against implicated officials, and review their relationship with China more broadly in light of the deepening abuses.”

items.title: Un passager intercepté dans un aéroport avec 100 boulettes de cocaïne dans l’estomac
items.description: Un ressortissant luso-guinéen de 40 ans a été interpellé, le lundi 2 novembre 2026, à l’aéroport international Osvaldo Vieira de Bissau, alors qu’il s’apprêtait à prendre un vol à destination du Portugal. Il transportait dans son organisme 100 boulettes de cocaïne, d’un poids total d’environ 1,138 kg, selon une information rendue publique ce jeudi 5 novembre par la Police judiciaire (PJ). L’opération a été menée par l’Unité nationale de lutte contre les drogues (UNCD), dans le cadre du dispositif de surveillance et de lutte contre le trafic international de stupéfiants au sein de l’infrastructure aéroportuaire. Le suspect devait embarquer à bord d’un vol pour Lisbonne, au Portugal, avec une escale à Casablanca, au Maroc, lorsqu’il a été intercepté par les enquêteurs. Les vérifications effectuées ont permis de découvrir que le quadragénaire dissimulait dans son corps 100 boulettes de cocaïne, représentant une quantité totale estimée à 1,138 kg. Cette technique de dissimulation, connue dans les réseaux de trafic de drogue, expose particulièrement les passeurs à de graves dangers. La rupture d'une seule des capsules dans l'organisme peut notamment provoquer une intoxication sévère et entraîner la mort. Présenté devant la juridiction compétente le mercredi 4 novembre, le mis en cause devait faire l’objet d’un premier interrogatoire et d’une évaluation en vue de la détermination de la mesure coercitive appropriée. À travers cette nouvelle interpellation, la Police judiciaire réaffirme sa volonté de renforcer la traque des réseaux criminels internationaux et d’empêcher que le territoire bissau-guinéen ne serve de couloir de transit pour l’acheminement de stupéfiants vers les marchés étrangers. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un passager intercepté dans un aéroport avec 100 boulettes de cocaïne dans l’estomac est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: I wait for trouble every morning at work, drop problems after work — Dangote
items.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou Africa’s richest industrialist, Aliko Dangote, has said he confronts business challenges as they arise but deliberately leaves work-related problems behind when returning home to maintain a balance between his professional and personal life. Dangote spoke while delivering the keynote address at the 25th anniversary celebration of Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ), where he urged women entrepreneurs to dream bigger, remain focused and develop the resilience to overcome business challenges. Sharing his approach to managing pressure, the business mogul said he starts each working day prepared to confront unexpected difficulties but makes a conscious effort not to carry them home. “Every morning, when I get to my office, I’m waiting for trouble to come. When it comes, I face it. When I finish in the evening, as soon as I get to my gate, I drop all my problems and enter my house,” he said. Speaking on the theme, ‘Rooted, Rising and Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World’, Dangote challenged women to raise their ambitions and pursue opportunities beyond their present achievements. “I’m challenging you to actually increase your ambition. You can get there. Dream big, do not dream small,” he said. He acknowledged that doing business in Nigeria came with significant challenges, including infrastructure deficits, high operating costs and difficulties accessing affordable long-term financing. He, however, urged entrepreneurs not to allow such obstacles to discourage them, stressing that success required determination, proper planning and the willingness to confront difficult situations. “There is nothing in life that is good that will come easy. If it is easy, everybody will be the same. You must say, yes, it’s difficult, but I can surmount all these challenges and I can do it,” he said. Reflecting on his business journey, Dangote recalled the financial difficulties encountered during the construction of the Obajana cement plant, particularly the high interest rates charged by banks at the time. He said the financing challenges put pressure on the company’s operations and expansion plans but did not deter it from pursuing its long-term vision. The industrialist also emphasised the importance of maintaining good health while managing business responsibilities, disclosing that he regularly monitors his blood pressure and adjusts his schedule when necessary. He urged entrepreneurs to learn how to manage pressure and avoid allowing business challenges to overwhelm their personal lives. Dangote attributed business success to vision, tenacity, focus and the ability to confront challenges without being overwhelmed by emotions. He also disclosed that the Dangote Group was expanding its operations beyond Nigeria, announcing plans to establish a $2.5 million caprolactam farm and production line in Namibia. He encouraged the women entrepreneurs to remain ambitious, carefully assess business opportunities and build enterprises capable of competing globally. “Business does not go with too much emotion,” he added. items.title: Dip Doundou Guiss : 2026, l’année de la double consécration
items.description: Après avoir pris part à la cérémonie d’ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, le rappeur Dip Doundou Guiss décroche deux certifications Disque d’or pour ses albums « LNN » (Loo Ñeme Ñakk) et « LFLF » (Lepp Fii Lañu Fekk). Une double distinction qui vient couronner une année particulièrement marquante dans son parcours musical. 2026 restera une année particulière dans la carrière de Dip Doundou Guiss. Le rappeur enchaîne les distinctions et confirme la portée de son univers musical. Après sa participation à la cérémonie des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, l’artiste signe une nouvelle performance avec l’obtention de deux certifications Disque d’or décernées par Africa Music & Charts (AMC). Les deux albums concernés sont « LNN » (Loo Ñeme Ñakk) et « LFLF » (Lepp Fii Lañu Fekk). Selon le barème communiqué par l’organisme certificateur, chacun de ces projets a dépassé le seuil de 5 000 équivalents ventes. Les certifications reposent sur les performances enregistrées sur les plateformes de streaming légal, conformément aux critères établis par AMC. Deux albums, deux Disques d’or Cette double distinction met en lumière les performances numériques de deux projets distincts de l'artiste. Au-delà de la reconnaissance discographique, elle témoigne de la présence grandissante du rap sénégalais sur les plateformes musicales et de sa capacité à toucher un public plus large. Avec deux albums certifiés au cours de la même année, Dip Doundou Guiss franchit ainsi une nouvelle étape dans sa carrière. Une performance qui contribue également à mettre en perspective l'évolution de l'industrie musicale sénégalaise, de plus en plus attentive aux indicateurs de consommation numérique. Le rap sur la scène des JOJ Cette reconnaissance musicale intervient dans une année également marquée par sa participation à la cérémonie des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026. Sa présence lors de cet événement sportif international a offert une vitrine au rap sénégalais, dans un contexte historique : Dakar accueille les premiers JOJ organisés sur le continent africain. La participation de l'artiste est par ailleurs présentée comme une première pour un artiste africain lors d'une cérémonie des JOJ. Un statut qui mérite toutefois d'être confirmé auprès de l'organisation avant publication. Entre visibilité internationale et reconnaissance discographique, Dip Doundou Guiss inscrit ainsi son parcours dans une année de consécration. Deux actualités qui, chacune à leur manière, mettent en lumière le rayonnement de la musique sénégalaise. A.N

items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a fini sur une note positive jeudi, son indice principal, le MASI, gagnant 3,33% à 17.317,91 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a progressé de 3,44% à 1.264,07 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody’s ESG Solutions, a pris 3,01% à 1.324,58 pts. De son côté, le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a avancé de 2,88% à 1.623,71 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Sociétés de portefeuilles – Holdings » (+9,78%), « Santé » (+5,84%) et « Télécommunications » (+5,21%) ont signé les meilleures performances. À l’inverse, seul le secteur « Boissons » (-0,12%) a terminé dans le rouge. Les échanges ont atteint plus de 1,01 milliard de dirhams (MMDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central et dominés par les transactions sur Douja Prom Addoha (59,97 MDH), TGCC (53,6 MDH) et Managem (39,3 MDH). items.description: The Ghana Football Association (GFA) has launched the maiden edition of the Kivo U-17 Regional Champions Cup as part of plans to strengthen grassroots football. The competition was launched at the GFA Secratariat on Thursday, November 5, providing another platform for emerging talents across the country. The 2026 Kivo U-17 Regional Champions Cup is scheduled to commence on November 8, with 13 teams expected to compete for laurels for the one-week tournament. The inaugural edition of the tournament will be played at the Ghanaman Soccer Centre of Excellence, bringing together regional U-17 champions. Speaking at the event, the GFA president, Kurt Okraku, described the competition as an important addition to the country’s youth football structure. “Today, we are not simply launching another football competition. We are unveiling an opportunity. An opportunity for young footballers across our regions to showcase their talent, compete at a higher level, represent their communities with pride and take another important step towards realising their football dreams,” Okraku said. “This is what grassroots football is about. It is about discovering talent, nurturing potential, creating opportunities and building the foundation upon which the future of Ghana football will stand.” Group A will comprise Raymond FC of the Ashanti Region, Sunyani Great Young Kotoko (Brong Ahafo), Show Show FC (Eastern), Tarkwa Barcelona FC (Western), Yaasin Colts FC (Upper West), Elite Academy-Achimota School (Greater Accra) and Elite Academy-Prempeh College (Ashanti). Group B will also feature Cheetah FC (Central), Desidero Football Academy (Greater Accra), Young Lions FC (Northern), Sogakope Cule FC (Volta), Bolga Soccer Masters (Upper East) and Elite Academy-Bolgatanga Senior High School (Upper East). The final of the tournament will be played on November 15.

items.title: Africa demands debt relief and direct finance at COP31 Climate Summit
items.description: The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN) has noted that the world’s transition away from fossil fuels cannot be called “just” if low- and middle-income nations must mortgage their economic futures to achieve it. Addressing delegates at the opening AGN plenary session at the 31st UN Climate Summit (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, the Executive Secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), Simon Stiell, declared that COP31 must mark a decisive pivot from commitment to execution. Stiell emphasised that the summit must turn existing international pledges into concrete action, lay the foundation for the second Global Stocktake (GST 2), and establish operational mechanisms to triple global climate finance. However, for African negotiators representing 54 nations on the front lines of severe climate shocks, the debate over scaling finance is inseparable from an escalating sovereign debt crisis that threatens to choke off the continent’s economic development. The macroeconomic reality confronting sub-Saharan Africa is increasingly precarious. While African nations account for less than half the per capita greenhouse gas emissions of the Global North, the region is experiencing severe weather disruptions, exacerbated by a climate change-fueled Super El Niño. At the same time, shrinking foreign aid and mounting sovereign debt obligations are severely curtailing domestic policy space. According to research presented by Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, Chair of the Africa Group of Negotiators, more than two-thirds of low-income countries are either already unable to meet their sovereign debt obligations or sit at high risk of debt distress. Rather than receiving concessional grant funding to build climate resilience, developing nations face international climate finance flows that predominantly increase their debt loads. Roughly two-thirds of all self-described climate finance provided by Global North nations consists of loans. This structural imbalance creates a destructive cycle. The top third most climate-vulnerable countries now spend an average of nearly two-thirds of their annual revenues servicing sovereign debt – spending, on average, 25 times more on debt servicing than on climate action. With borrowing costs for African nations averaging 13 per cent, sovereign debt service has become the primary barrier to clean energy transitions and climate adaptation. The macroeconomic crisis translates directly into governance bottlenecks across sub-Saharan Africa, where governments are forced to choose between basic civic services and debt compliance. Country-level evidence submitted to the AGN plenary highlights how sovereign debt disincentivises clean energy deployment and disrupts local administration. In Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, fossil fuels comprised almost 90 per cent of export value in 2024. Despite legacy oil and gas extraction projects continuing to plague local communities, geopolitical conflict in the Middle East drove up global petroleum prices. Rather than providing capital for clean energy reinvestment, mounting debt burdens have disincentivised Nigeria’s transition away from fossil fuel exports. As AGN Chair Antwi-Boasiako Amoah stressed during the plenary, African populations will not tolerate diplomatic climate agreements that require sacrificing foundational domestic development—including healthcare systems, primary schools, municipal infrastructure, and local roads—to solve a global climate crisis to which Africa barely contributed. African nations arrive at COP31 having demonstrated substantial climate ambition within their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). Sub-Saharan Africa holds the world’s largest concentration of renewable energy targets embedded within national climate plans. However, up to 90 per cent of that planned ambition remains contingent on international financial support that remains unsecured. To bridge this gap, the African Group of Negotiators has organised its negotiating agenda around three core demands: Predictable, substantial climate capital that reflects the true magnitude of NDC implementation costs across African economies; A decisive shift away from sovereign loans toward grant-based and concessional finance that does not worsen fiscal distress; and Channelling climate funds directly through African financial institutions, national entities, and regional development mechanisms to ensure localised governance and rapid deployment. For African negotiators, the outcome at COP31 transcends energy metrics. As Chair Antwi-Boasiako Amoah has noted, a just energy transition is fundamentally about whether Africa can industrialise, create decent employment, and extend electricity access to the hundreds of millions of citizens currently without power. With Ethiopia designated to host COP32, the African Group has signalled that sovereign debt relief and non-debt climate finance will remain the central test of international climate justice.

FG warns tertiary institutions against exploitative PPP deals
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has warned federal universities, polytechnics and other tertiary institutions against entering into Public-Private Partnership (PPP) agreements that prioritise investors’ profits over students’ welfare. It insisted that affordability, accessibility and public interest must remain central to education-sector partnerships, warning that projects beyond students’ financial reach would defeat the purpose of such arrangements. The Director Overseeing the Office of the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, Dr Folake David, gave the warning in Abuja while declaring open a two-day annual PPP Forum for Desk Officers in Federal Tertiary Institutions. David challenged institutions to develop viable and bankable projects capable of attracting private investment without compromising their public-service responsibilities. She said education-sector partnerships would only be considered successful if they delivered measurable social benefits, improved learning outcomes and affordable services, rather than merely maximising returns for private investors. The forum, organised by the Federal Ministry of Education in collaboration with the Nigerian Institute of Infrastructure and Public-Private Partnership (NIIP), was themed, “Public-Private Partnership: Bridging the Gap Between Policy, Investment and Sustainable Implementation.” David said the theme reflected a major challenge facing the education sector, noting that although the government had established policy frameworks and investors had expressed interest, translating both into viable projects remained a major hurdle. She explained that the government could no longer shoulder the enormous financial burden of providing laboratories, students’ hostels, workshops, high-capacity centres, theatres and other essential infrastructure in tertiary institutions, particularly amid competing national demands and dwindling public resources. According to her, PPP arrangements offer opportunities to mobilise private capital, technical expertise, innovation and management capacity to complement government funding and accelerate infrastructure development. She, however, cautioned that such partnerships must not become avenues for exploiting students or commercialising essential educational services beyond their reach. The ministry official urged PPP Desk Officers to move beyond routine administrative responsibilities and become investment scouts, project facilitators and custodians of public interest. She challenged them to identify viable investment opportunities, prepare bankable proposals and engage credible private-sector partners, expressing the expectation that the forum would produce a pipeline of sustainable, education-focused projects rather than end with mere resolutions. Also speaking, a representative of the Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Mr Akwu Okolo, disclosed that the commission had reduced the time required to review and certify PPP projects from about 60 days to seven days. Okolo, who represented the Director-General, Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh, said the commission had also issued 13 PPP guidelines to facilitate implementation of presidentially approved project approval thresholds. He urged tertiary institutions to identify investment opportunities based on their specific needs and develop credible proposals capable of attracting investors. He noted that although some social infrastructure projects might not be financially self-sustaining, their importance to the government’s social contract with citizens made them indispensable. Earlier, the Director, Special Duties Department, Federal Ministry of Education, Mr Murtala Alhaji Tanko, described the forum as a strategic platform for strengthening institutional capacity and translating government policies into concrete investment opportunities. Tanko identified inadequate infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms, insufficient teaching and learning facilities, and poor access to modern technology as persistent challenges undermining the quality of education in tertiary institutions. He urged participants to develop practical recommendations backed by clear priorities, assigned responsibilities and implementation strategies. He said their responsibilities included identifying and preparing projects, ensuring regulatory compliance, facilitating stakeholder engagement and monitoring implementation to guarantee measurable improvements in educational infrastructure and services. In a goodwill message delivered on behalf of the Director, Colleges of Education Department, Dr Uchenna Uba, the Deputy Director, Mrs Vivian Oluwatobi Luke, said PPPs could help modernise lecture halls, students’ hostels, laboratories, workshops, ICT facilities and renewable energy infrastructure. She, however, stressed the need for sound project preparation, transparency, accountability and effective monitoring to ensure that the partnerships delivered lasting benefits. Luke urged participants to translate the knowledge acquired at the forum into sustainable arrangements capable of strengthening teaching, learning and skills development. Similarly, the Director, Polytechnic Education and Allied Institutions Department, Mrs Igwe Amy, called for stronger private-sector participation in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). She said industry partnerships were critical to improving the quality of technical education, providing relevant skills and preparing graduates for labour market demands. Amy urged PPP Desk Officers to familiarise themselves with the regulatory framework and develop transparent, mutually beneficial and bankable projects to strengthen technical institutions. Reaffirming the ministry’s commitment to the initiative, David said the Federal Government would continue to promote transparent, accountable and value-driven partnerships to complement ongoing education reforms. The post FG warns tertiary institutions against exploitative PPP deals appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dapaong/Education : 1 585 élèves-professeurs de la 5è promotion de l’ENFPE entament leur formation
items.description: Dapaong, 5 nov. (ATOP) – Le ministre de l’Education nationale, Mama Omorou, a lancé l’année académique 2026-2028 de la 5 è promotion des Elèves professeurs d’école (EPE), le jeudi 5 novembre à l’Ecole normale de formation des professeurs d’école (ENFPE) de Dapaong. Cette promotion compte 1.585 apprenants appelés à se faire former pour l’enseignement préscolaire et primaire. Le ministre a indiqué que la formation des enseignants constitue un investissement stratégique pour le développement et la souveraineté nationale. Il a rappelé que la création des ENFPE s’inscrit dans la volonté du gouvernement de professionnaliser le métier d’enseignant, d’améliorer la qualité de la formation initiale et de promouvoir l’excellence dans le système éducatif. Présentant le bilan de cette réforme engagée depuis 2018 , le ministre Omorou a fait savoir qu’au total 10.684 EPE ont été formés, à savoir 6.114 femmes (57%) contre 4.570 hommes. Il a indiqué que 75% des admis au concours national de recrutement des fonctionnaires enseignants en 2026 sont des élèves-professeurs issus des ENFPE contre 25% en 2024. Le ministre a assigné aux élèves de la nouvelle promotion, trois principales exigences : la maîtrise du numérique comme outil d’amélioration des pratiques pédagogiques, la résilience à travers la fabrication de matériels didactiques à partir de ressources locales et l’adoption d’une démarche d’enseignant-chercheur fondée sur la créativité, l’innovation et l’esprit critique. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence des autorités administratives dont le secrétaire général du gouvernorat des Savanes, Kégbéro Latifou, politiques et traditionnelles, des responsables du ministère de l’Education nationale, des acteurs du système éducatif et des partenaires techniques et financiers. Elle a été marquée, entre autres, par une conférence inaugurale sur le thème : « Le professionnalisme, l’excellence et les valeurs citoyennes, socle de compétences du professeur d’école » et des prestations de la chorale de l’ENFPE. items.title: Ghana seeks deeper Chinese investment in mining and mineral processing
items.description: Ghana is seeking to expand its mining partnership with China, with a renewed push for investment in mineral processing, technology transfer and exploration as part of efforts to retain more value from the country’s natural resources. Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Sulemana Yusif, led a Ghanaian delegation to meet the Vice-Chairperson of the People’s Government of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Sui Guohua, in Nanning on Thursday, November 5, ahead of the China-ASEAN (Guangxi) Mining Cooperation Conference. The discussions centred on strengthening relations between the two sides and identifying investment opportunities in mineral exploration, industrial development, technology transfer and local value addition. Mr Sui highlighted Guangxi’s expertise in industry and mineral processing, expressing interest in expanding cooperation with Ghana in mineral development and related industrial ventures. The engagement was also marked by a welcoming banquet for the Ghanaian delegation. Presenting Ghana’s investment prospects, Mr Yusif pointed to the country’s deposits of gold, bauxite, iron ore, graphite, lithium and manganese, describing the minerals as important resources for its economic development. He disclosed that mining contributed approximately 9.98 per cent to Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product in 2025, while gold production reached a record 5.94 million ounces. This placed Ghana sixth among the world’s leading gold producers and maintained its position as Africa’s largest gold producer. The Deputy Minister called for expanded cooperation in mineral processing, geological exploration, technical expertise, skills development and responsible small-scale mining. He also highlighted the need for stronger environmental protection measures and increased Ghanaian participation across the mining value chain. He said Ghana’s ambition was not limited to increasing mineral output but also included developing local industries, creating jobs and ensuring that a greater share of the economic benefits from its mineral resources remained within the country. The engagements are expected to provide a platform for translating the shared interests of Ghana and China into practical investment and technical partnerships. Mr Yusif reaffirmed the government’s readiness to work with international investors seeking opportunities in the country’s mining industry.

items.title: Troops kill three suspected kidnappers, recover four rifles in Kogi
items.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja Troops of the Nigerian Army, in collaboration with the Kogi State Vigilance Service (KSVS), have killed three suspected kidnappers and recovered four AK-47 rifles and a cache of ammunition during an operation in Igalamela/Odolu Local Government Area of Kogi State. The operation, conducted on November 4, followed earlier raids on suspected kidnappers’ hideouts in Edimogbo Forest, as security operatives extended their search towards the Obele Forest area in pursuit of fleeing suspects. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lieutenant Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement, saying the suspects attempted to escape on sighting the advancing troops, leading to an exchange of fire in which three of them were killed. Items recovered during the operation included four AK-47 rifles, 12 magazines, 336 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three bandoliers and an identity card. The statement said the operation was part of sustained efforts by troops of the 12 Composite Brigade, under the newly established 5 Division of the Nigerian Army, to dismantle kidnapping networks and deny criminal elements safe havens in Kogi State. It added that continued offensive operations, intelligence-driven patrols and searches of identified criminal hideouts were aimed at restricting the movement of kidnappers and restoring confidence among residents of affected communities. The Commander, 12 Composite Brigade, Brigadier General Kasim Umar Sidi, commended the troops and personnel of the Kogi State Vigilance Service for their resilience, professionalism and effectiveness during the operation. He urged them to sustain the momentum and ensure that criminal elements were denied freedom of action within the Brigade’s area of responsibility. The Army also appealed to residents of Kogi State and neighbouring communities to provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing operations. items.title: Finding Love in Accra Episode 5: Dinner and other miscalculations
items.description: Read Also: Finding Love In Accra Episode 4: Let me hear your voice By Saturday evening, I had shaved things that had no appointment. Let me confess early so we can all be disappointed in me together. I went to dinner without panties. The dress was fitted. Underwear would show. That was the explanation I gave myself while standing in front of the mirror. There were seamless options in the drawer. I closed it. All week, Kojo and I had been talking. Small messages in the morning. Calls that lasted longer than either of us intended. Once, he said my name so quietly that I asked him to repeat himself even though I had heard him perfectly. Now he was coming to my apartment for dinner. My suggestion. “Restaurants are noisy,” I had told him. Apparently, I required absolute silence to ask a man about his week. At seven fifteen, my doorbell rang. Kojo stood outside holding a bottle of wine, wearing a dark shirt that fitted him with unnecessary precision. “You look beautiful.” “Thank you.” I stepped aside. His hand touched my waist as he passed. A brief, ordinary touch. My body received it as correspondence. Dinner was lovely, which made everything worse. He liked the food. Asked for more. Helped carry the plates into the kitchen despite my protests. Then he stood beside me at the sink, drying a glass while I washed. Domestic behaviour. Very dangerous when you have already imagined where somebody might keep his shoes. “You’re quiet,” he said. “Just tired.” I had enough energy to power Tema. He took the glass from my hand. “Leave these. You cooked.” We settled on the sofa, closer than necessary because I had placed the wine at one end and the cushions at the other. I had organised the seating like an event planner with a personal agenda. For a while, we talked easily. Then his phone lit up on the coffee table. Nana I looked away so quickly I nearly injured my neck. He silenced it. “Sorry.” “Won’t you answer?” “I’ll call her back.” Her. I lifted my glass. “The lady from the restaurant?” “Yes.” Something in his voice made me put the glass down carefully. “Who is she?” “My girlfriend.” I nodded. Once. Then again, as if he had explained a parking arrangement. “Oh.” The room became painfully detailed. The hum of my fridge. A drop of water on his sleeve. My own bare legs crossed beneath a dress that suddenly felt much too short. “You have a girlfriend?” “Yes.” “And you didn’t think to mention that?” He turned towards me. “I thought you knew.” “How would I know, Kojo?” “You saw us together. And you introduced me as—” “Please don’t say, brother.” He stopped. I pulled a cushion onto my lap. For warmth. For dignity. For the entire situation. “Lovia,” he said slowly, “what did you think tonight was?” There are questions a person should answer while fully dressed underneath. I looked at the bottle on the table. “You asked me to dinner.” “And you invited me here.” “Yes. Because I thought…” I couldn’t finish. His expression changed. “Oh.” “Yes,” I said. “Oh.” He leaned back and rubbed his jaw. “I should have answered you when you asked about her.” “You laughed.” “I know.” “You knew I was asking for a reason.” He looked at me. “Yes,” he admitted. That hurt more than I expected. “So why let me keep guessing?” For once, he had no quick reply. “I liked hearing from you again,” he said eventually. “I didn’t want to make it awkward.” “Well. Excellent work.” He looked down. “I’m sorry.” I believed him. It did not make me feel less foolish. He left a few minutes later, taking his warmth, his lovely shoulders and the possibility I had built around both. I locked the door and stood with my forehead against it. Then I called Emefa. “How was dinner?” she asked. “He has a girlfriend.” Silence. “Lovia.” “I know.” “Did you ask before tonight?” “I tried.” “What do you mean, you tried?” I walked into my bedroom. Opened the drawer. Put on panties. “Emefa, please. I cannot explain all my decisions at once.” To be continued.
