items.title: Hamile curfew revised to 10 pm–4 am, effective November 5
items.description: The government has revised the curfew imposed on Hamile Township and its surrounding communities in the Lambussie District of the Upper West Region, setting the new restriction hours from 10:00 pm to 4:00 am. The curfew was initially from 6:00 pm to 5:00 am. The revised curfew takes effect on Thursday, November 5, 2026, following a review by the Minister for the Interior, acting on the advice of the National Security Council and through an Executive Instrument. The adjustment is expected to regulate movement during the designated hours as authorities work to maintain peace and security in the area. In a statement issued on Thursday, November 5, the government urged chiefs, opinion leaders, the youth and residents to exercise restraint amid the challenges confronting the area. It also appealed to community members to use peaceful and non-violent means to express their grievances and contribute to restoring and maintaining peace. Meanwhile, the government has maintained a total ban on the possession of arms, ammunition and other offensive weapons by anyone in Hamile Township and its surrounding communities. It warned that anyone found in possession of such weapons would be arrested and prosecuted. The measures form part of efforts by the government to address security concerns in the area and prevent further disturbances. Residents and other stakeholders have been urged to comply with the curfew and weapons restrictions to support the restoration of lasting peace and stability in the community.

items.title: Kozah/Enregistrement biométrique : le préfet s’assure du déroulement de l’opération dans les quatre communes
items.description: Kozah, 5 nov. (ATOP) – Le préfet de la Kozah, Colonel Bonfoh Faré a effectué, le mercredi 4 novembre, une tournée de supervision de l’opération d’enregistrement biométrique dans les quatre communes de la préfecture. Il a été accompagné d’une délégation multisectorielle dont les responsables de l’Agence nationale d’identification (ANID) et de l’Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques et démographiques (INSEED)- Kara. L’objectif est de s’assurer du bon déroulement de l’opération, de la mobilisation des agents recenseurs et de recueillir les éventuelles difficultés. Il a été également question de rappeler l’importance de cette opération et d’exhorter les chefs traditionnels et autres acteurs impliqués à renforcer la sensibilisation afin qu’aucun citoyen de la préfecture ne soit laissé pour compte. La délégation s’est successivement rendue à l’Ecole primaire public (EPP) Atchangbadè (Kozah 4), à l’EPP Awandjélo (Kozah 3), aux lycées Kara Sud et Kara 2 (Kozah1) et à l’EPP Pya centrale (Kozah2). Dans chaque centre visité, le préfet a échangé avec les agents recenseurs, les autorités communales et traditionnelles et ceux chargés de la gestion des plaintes. Il a souligné que l’opération se déroule bien avec tout le dispositif, notamment les kits et le matériel d’enregistrement mis en place avec la présence effective des autorités locales sur les lieux. Cependant, des difficultés liées à l’insuffisance du matériel, au retard de la population qui n’arrive que dans la soirée ont été relevés. Selon un encadreur, cette affluence dans l’après-midi s’explique par le fait que les populations sont occupées par les activités champêtres dans la matinée. Le préfet Bonfo a relevé l’importance de cette opération invitant les agents à réserver un bon accueil à tous sans exception. Il a interpellé les premiers responsables de l’opération dans la Kozah à prendre des mesures au regard des observations et qu’une attention particulière soit accordée aux personnes vivant avec un handicap. Le préfet a exhorté les autorités communales, traditionnelles et tous les acteurs impliqués dans l’opération à redoubler d’effort dans la mobilisation de la population pour l’atteinte des objectifs. Le chef de mission dans la Kozah, Bleoussi Joseph a promis de remonter toutes les difficultés rencontrées afin de trouver des solutions idoines et garantir l’atteinte des résultats escomptés. Quand au directeur régional de l’éducation de la Kara, Bograh Badjaglana, il a réitéré son engagement de prendre des dispositions avec les chefs d’établissement afin que tous les élèves soient enregistrés. Cette opération d’enregistrement biométrique s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet d’intégration régionale et d’inclusion en Afrique de l’Ouest, piloté par l’ANID avec l’appui technique de l’INSEED. Elle permettra à chaque Togolais de disposer d’une carte e-ID permettant d’accéder à tous les services publics et financiers. ATOP/TAL/BA/BV

items.title: ‘We Did This for This Man?’
items.description: I t was the morning after the midterm elections, and Jeff Flake couldn’t stop laughing. Not necessarily a mean laugh—Flake, who is preternaturally good-humored, tends to chuckle amiably through most conversations. But I thought I detected a quantum of vindication or glee in the voice of the former senator from Arizona. I’d called Flake to ask what he made of his party’s historic electoral meltdown. “It feels literally like a 10-year fever just broke,” he told me. “I’ve been saying to my wife, It’ll break. It’ll break , and she’s been saying, When? When? When? And it looks like it has.” During the first Trump administration, Flake distinguished himself as one of Capitol Hill’s most outspoken Republican critics of the president—of his character, his policies, and his coarsening of America’s political culture. Flake was heartbroken by his party’s craven accommodation of Donald Trump and routinely called it out. “One day in the not too distant future,” he’d predicted in 2019 , “Republicans will wake up and say, ‘We did this for this man?’” Flake believes that day has finally arrived. “Republicans have to be asking themselves, ‘What did we get out of this?’” he said. “Twelve trillion dollars added to the national debt during the two Trump terms so far? Our trade deals in tatters? Our allies don’t trust us? China has not been restrained?” Yes, Flake conceded, the border has been secured (though many of Trump’s immigration policies could be undone by a swipe of his successor’s pen). And yes, the Supreme Court now has a conservative majority (though any Republican president would have achieved that, and the current 6–3 majority owes more to Senator Mitch McConnell than to Trump). But the trade-off for even these qualified accomplishments, Flake argued, has been that “the party has lost its soul.” He pointed to the “sickening” crony capitalism that dominates the president’s orbit, and to the GOP’s continued support for Trump’s claims that the 2020 election was stolen. [ Eugene Robinson: The end of the Trump era ] And now, after thoroughly remaking the party in his image and purging it of anti-MAGA dissidents such as Flake, Trump has handed his party a generationally devastating midterm wipeout. “That’s what I think Republicans looking in the mirror are saying: ‘We did this for this man? Was it worth it?’” I reminded him that one of those Republicans, former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy, once derided Flake’s principled resistance to Trump as feckless and self-defeating. No one is putting up statues of Jeff Flake in the Capitol, McCarthy had sneered in an interview with my colleague Mark Leibovich . (It bears mentioning that McCarthy said this in between licks of a chocolate-ice-cream cone while showing off pictures of himself on Air Force One. It bears further mentioning that McCarthy was shortly thereafter stripped of the speakership and defenestrated from Congress while Trump passively watched.) I asked Flake whether he now sees McCarthy’s MAGA chest-thumping in a new light, given the GOP’s electoral collapse. He laughed again. “I’m not sure many statues are going to be erected to anybody who was part of this,” he said. Forgive the Never Trump Republican a little gloating this week. It’s been a long decade. E leven years ago, when Trump first entered the presidential race, critics such as Flake—who regarded the reality-TV host as a dangerous, know-nothing con man—composed the great majority of the GOP establishment. But once Trump started rising in the polls, winning races, and accumulating power, the number of Republicans willing to acknowledge the emperor’s nakedness rapidly dwindled. Those elected officials, political strategists, and conservative commentators who remained clear-eyed arrayed themselves under the “Never Trump” banner. In op-eds and interviews, they tried to persuade their fellow Republicans to return to their senses. They railed against Trump’s malformed psyche and broken moral compass. And almost all of them, at various points, made dire predictions about the consequences of their party’s affiliation with Trump. For a long time, those predictions did not look especially prescient—not in November 2016, when Trump shocked the world with his upset victory, and not in 2024, when he stormed back into office despite the many political obituaries that had already been written about him. But the devout core of the Never Trump faithful clung to their belief that Trump’s political project would eventually collapse and bury his party in the process. On Tuesday night, they got to see their prophecies fulfilled. “Trump has brought a Chernobyl level disaster to the Republican Party tonight,” Mike Murphy, a Republican consultant who advised former Florida Governor Jeb Bush’s primary campaign in 2016, posted on X. “Tonight the Trump Show was finally cancelled. #BoxOfficePoison.” [ Adam Serwer: Even where MAGA won, MAGA lost ] “Bad policy, bad character make bad politics,” Mitt Romney, who as Utah’s junior senator voted twice to impeach Trump, posted on X. “Hoping for a course correction, for the country and for my party.” Joe Walsh, a former Republican representative from Illinois who supported Trump in 2016 before turning on him and leaving the party, posted on Bluesky, “No political party and no president have ever deserved an electoral thumping and a complete political repudiation more than this political party and this president deserve.” Mark Sanford, the former representative from South Carolina who mounted a quixotic bid for the Republican nomination in 2020, told Semafor that Tuesday night was “a Waterloo moment for Trump.” In his newsletter, Adam Kinzinger, another representative driven from office for his opposition to Trump, effused alliteratively about the comprehensive beatdown his erstwhile colleagues took on Tuesday: “They got spanked in Senate races. Hammered in House races. Gutted in governors races. And lit up in legislative races.” Bill Kristol, the neoconservative former editor of the Weekly Standard magazine, which died during Trump’s first term, was moved to quote Thomas Paine and Alexander Hamilton while declaring, “Election Day 2026 was the true celebration of our 250th anniversary.” The mood in the Never Trump media seemed to hover somewhere between ebullient and bloodthirsty. In The Bulwark , a publication founded by Weekly Standard alumni, Jonathan Last celebrated the prospect of pursuing charges against the alleged crooks and criminals in the president’s orbit. “ Lawyer up, bitches,” he wrote, before listing various categories of people who may soon face congressional scrutiny, including Trump donors, business partners, and DOGE employees. “I’m going to give you the best free legal advice you’re ever getting in your life: Get a great fucking criminal defense lawyer. You’re gonna need it.” Meanwhile, at The Dispatch , another redoubt of Never Trump conservatism, editors were exultant but restrained. “The electorate has rendered its judgment of Donald Trump his MAGA-fied Republican Party: No more ,” they wrote in an editorial that welcomed the coming GOP civil war. “The fight for the right starts now.” N ot every Republican who pegged Trump as a corrosive, party-destroying force was celebrating vindication. When I called Peter Meijer, who served a term in the House representing Michigan’s Third Congressional district, he seemed to be in a contemplative mood. “I think my ratio of condolence to congratulations calls was about 10 to one,” he told me. Meijer is not a Never Trumper. He has voted for the president, and supports many of his policies. But after January 6, 2021, Meijer committed MAGA apostasy by voting to impeach Trump. He lost his next primary to a far-right MAGA devotee. But he told me that Tuesday’s election ended the careers of some genuinely good public servants. “Looking at the class I came into Congress with, a lot of whom are reasonable, good, governing types—they just got wiped out in this wave.” His voice took on a poetic tone. “Swept out to sea as the tsunami receded.” Meijer seemed less eager than others to indulge in Trumpenfreude . He was worried about Democratic overreach. And he noted that the president’s doomsayers had been wrong plenty of times before. But when I asked him what he thought of Trump’s claim that Republicans lost only because Trump himself wasn’t on the ballot, Meijer seemed to lose his patience. “This was an anti-Republican wave, and he’s the leader of the Republican Party,” he told me. He went on to cite all of the ways that Trump had hamstrung his party—the refusal to develop legislative relationships in Congress; his unseemly cryptocurrency profiteering; and the appearance of corruption in much of his other dealmaking while in office. He sighed. “It’s like, what the hell are we doing, guys?”

items.title: Midterms over, Democrats plunge into wide-open 2028 presidential race
items.description: With the US midterms over, Democrats are turning to what could become one of their most crowded and unpredictable presidential primaries in decades, a 2028 contest likely to expose the party’s divide over how to win back the White House. No Democrat has emerged as a clear favourite in a field that could attract dozens of contenders, while Republicans have a smaller group of widely discussed candidates, led by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, to succeed President Donald Trump, who is constitutionally barred from seeking a third term. Potential Democratic candidates, including sitting governors and senators, have spent months cultivating donors, visiting states with early nominating contests and raising their national profiles, positioning themselves for a race that strategists expect to begin in earnest now that the midterms are over. The sweeping victories by Democrats on Tuesday, when voters delivered a sharp rebuke to Trump and his agenda, will intensify discussions within both parties about how to win over an electorate unhappy with the country’s direction. Supporters react to early election results in favour of US Senator Jon Ossoff at an election night watch party hosted by the Democratic Party of Georgia after the midterm election in Atlanta, Georgia on November 3, 2026. — AFP Despite their resounding victories on Tuesday, Democrats enter the 2028 campaign still divided over whether to tack to the centre or move further left on issues ranging from healthcare and taxes to policing and foreign policy. Republican candidates will face a different challenge: how to distance themselves from Trump after Tuesday’s repudiation of his policies. They need to broaden their appeal beyond the president’s base while avoiding a break with the populist Make America Great Again movement that has come to define the party. Trump, who has dominated the political landscape for a decade, may be reluctant to yield centre stage, and his continued influence with MAGA followers could complicate the path of the party’s next standard-bearer. Looming Democratic battle Doug Sosnik, a Democratic strategist, said both progressives and moderates will claim vindication in their ideological approaches, ensuring an intense internal battle over the party’s future as the 2028 race begins in earnest. One of the most high-profile progressive wins came in the Michigan Senate contest, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed easily defeated Republican Mike Rogers in a likely 2028 presidential swing state, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. “All kinds of wings of the Democratic Party can find affirmation in the results last night,” Sosnik said on Wednesday. “I don’t think that anyone can, nor should they, try to contain the differences we have as a party.” Several potential candidates have either acknowledged considering a White House run or declined to rule one out. Most spent the final weeks of the midterm campaign stumping for fellow Democrats in early nominating states such as Nevada, New Hampshire and South Carolina. They include former Vice President Kamala Harris, who lost to Trump in 2024, Governors Gavin Newsom of California and Andy Beshear of Kentucky, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York, a leading progressive voice. California Governor Gavin Newsom speaks during a media preview day at the California Science Center for its new Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center in Los Angeles, California, the US on October 28, 2026. — Reuters/File Reuters contacted representatives for nine of the party’s most prominent potential contenders. None confirmed a 2028 run. Nine days after the November 3 elections, several prospective Democratic candidates, including Buttigieg and another progressive, US Representative Ro Khanna of California, are scheduled to attend a gathering in Denver hosted by Majority Democrats. The group, backed largely by moderate Democrats and billionaire donor Steve Mandel, advocates for younger party leaders and a party platform that is more centrist. US Representative Jake Auchincloss of Massachusetts, the group’s chair, said the event is meant to spark a debate about the party’s future before the 2028 race takes shape, and lay out a positive agenda for what the party is for, rather than just being anti-Trump. Scott Ferson, a Democratic strategist, said the party’s presidential primary could attract a huge number of candidates. “There are at least 30 Democrats who are saying to people close to them, ‘Do you think I should run?’” Ferson said. Republicans in Trump’s shadow By contrast, Republican 2028 hopefuls have been more guarded, mostly staying in Trump’s shadow and deferential to him. That could now change after Tuesday night’s rout in which voters expressed deep dissatisfaction with Trump’s handling of the economy and foreign policy and demanded more action against government corruption. Vance is in a particularly difficult position, said Matt Dole, a Republican strategist. Vance has less freedom than other potential 2028 Republican contenders to put daylight between himself and Trump because he is vice president, a role that traditionally involves defending the president and his policies. “Vance just doesn’t have the wiggle room that somebody else in the cabinet has, who can resign,” Dole said. US Vice President JD Vance speaks at a midterm campaign rally at JRJ Construction in Weatherford, Texas, the US on October 29, 2026. — AFP/File Still, Vance acknowledged on Wednesday that the war in Iran, which Trump launched in February and which is deeply unpopular among Americans, had cost Republicans the election. That, however, did not represent a clear break with Trump, who made a similar acknowledgement on Tuesday night. Whoever emerges within the Republican Party as its new standard-bearer will face the task of keeping Trump’s ‘Make America Great Again’ (MAGA) base onside while rebuilding the broader coalition that powered his 2024 victory. Exit polls on Tuesday showed that key constituencies of that coalition, including younger voters, Hispanics and some Black men, had deserted Republicans. Vance has said there is “a chance” he will not run, citing family considerations, while Rubio has said he has “no plans at this time” to seek the presidency. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, who unsuccessfully sought the Republican presidential nomination against Trump in 2024, has declined to rule out another White House bid. Other Republicans viewed as potential candidates include Arkansas Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders and US Senator Ted Cruz of Texas.

items.title: Six dead and others injured in fire at New York City building
items.description: Six people have died after a large fire broke out in a residential building in Brooklyn, New York City, officials say. Several others were hurt in the blaze, which occurred early on Thursday morning, the New York City Fire Department (FDNY) said in a statement. More than 230 fire and emergency medical personnel were sent to the scene near Sunset Park after the fire was first reported at around 01:40 local time (06:40 GMT). Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was “heartbroken” by the deaths, and has asked New Yorkers to “take a moment to pray for the full recovery of those who were injured”. The cause of the blaze is being investigated. A crew specialising in hazardous materials was sent to the scene because of the presence of a lithium-ion battery, although it was not clear whether this was linked to the blaze. The emergency responders reportedly discovered on their arrival that the building’s first and second floors had been engulfed by flames. Four individuals were pronounced dead at the scene, according to the FDNY. A male and female were also taken to the hospital, where they were pronounced dead, the New York City Police Department (NYPD) said. items.title: Mother and daughter die after suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada
items.description: A mother and daughter have died after a suspected grizzly bear attack in the Canadian province of British Columbia, their family has announced. The women – identified as Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20 -were reported missing on 1 November when they did not return from what was supposed to be a short afternoon walk, the family said. Their remains were found in a trail area in Bella Coola, according to the BC Conservation Officer Service (BCCOS), which said evidence at the scene “suggested an animal may have been involved”. Conservation officers are working to track down any bears involved. Balcarras’ remains were found on Monday and Reed’s on Tuesday during search efforts by conservation officers and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the BCCOS, said it was not yet clear if more than one was potentially involved in the women’s deaths. He added that any captured bear would be assessed and if it is found to have been involved in the attack “it will be dispatched in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety”. Balcarras and Reed were “two peas in a pod” who “got along really, really well” and shared many hobbies, Balcarras’ brother, Josh Balcarras, told CBC. “When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her,” he said. Balcarras had recently moved to Bella Coola to pursue a new career and begin a new chapter in her life, according to an online fundraiser to help the family with funeral costs. Grizzly bears are listed as a species of “special concern” under federal legislation, and are an important part of the British Columbia landscape, according to Environmental Reporting BC . Between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears are estimated to live in the province, according to the province’s Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, which has classified them as vulnerable. According to the ministry, conflicts between bears and humans are “relatively rare” unless the animals are startled or protecting their cubs and food. But there have been a number of attacks in British Columbia in recent years. A grizzly bear injured two hikers in the McGregor Mountain area in October 2025, one of whom died later due to critical injuries. The bear was later found dead. The following month, a bear attacked a school group – also in the Bella Coola area – injuring 11 people. The BC Wildlife Federation (BCWF) has said that reports of grizzly-human conflicts have risen since the province introduced a ban on hunting grizzly bears for sport in 2017. “With no hunting pressure, grizzlies and humans will increasingly occupy the same spaces with inevitable consequences,” the BCWF’s executive director Jesse Zeman said at the time.

Afienya: Tipper truck drivers accuse military personnel of shooting and assaulting members
items.description: The National Sand and Stone Tipper Truck Drivers Association has accused some military personnel of shooting and physically assaulting its members during an operation at Afienya in the Greater Accra Region. The alleged incident has left several people injured, with some reportedly in critical condition and receiving treatment at the Tema General Hospital. The association claims the security personnel also subjected truck operators and some residents to excessive physical abuse, seized their mobile phones and impounded and damaged several tipper trucks during the operation. According to the Greater Accra Regional Vice-Chairman of the association, Abdul-Moomen Mohammed, popularly known as Kowa Naso, some of the association’s members have been prevented from accessing their businesses despite holding valid licences and permits to operate. He said the affected operators had obtained the necessary clearance from the Ningo-Prampram District Assembly but were still being subjected to what the association considers excessive military action. The allegations come amid growing concerns over the conduct of security personnel deployed to enforce restrictions on sand-winning activities, with similar complaints previously raised by tipper truck operators in the Ningo-Prampram area. The association is demanding an investigation into the alleged shootings, assault and destruction of property, insisting that operators engaged in legitimate business activities should not be subjected to violence. It is also appealing to President John Dramani Mahama to intervene and ensure that the rights and safety of licensed operators are protected. The association says it expects the authorities to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and hold any personnel found culpable accountable. Meanwhile, the Member of Parliament for the area, who doubles as the Minister of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has called on the Chief of Defence Staff to take disciplinary action against the military officers for the alleged inaction. items.title: 2027: Police assure corps members, ad hoc staff of protection
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has assured members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and other ad hoc staff to be engaged by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of adequate protection during the 2027 general elections. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, gave the assurance at a joint media briefing of the Forum of Security and Intelligence Agencies, organised by the Office of the National Security Adviser. He was responding to concerns over reported abductions of corps members in different parts of the country, particularly as they are expected to form a significant part of INEC’s ad hoc workforce during the elections. Iniedu said the police had conducted an extensive threat assessment and were strengthening security arrangements to protect electoral personnel and materials and ensure the smooth conduct of the polls. He said the arrangements would be implemented in collaboration with other security agencies before, during and after the elections. “In every election cycle, there are potential threats to soft targets. However, as other targets become increasingly fortified by security agencies, criminals may attempt to exploit perceived vulnerabilities elsewhere. “The Nigeria Police Force has conducted an extensive threat assessment ahead of the forthcoming general elections, and we are adequately preparing for the challenges. “During the Osun State election, for instance, we engaged corps members, their parents and other stakeholders and assured them of our commitment to providing adequate security for all ad hoc personnel. We came out unscathed. The forthcoming general election will not be an exception,” he said. The police spokesman said the force was working with sister security agencies and engaging INEC to strengthen protection for corps members and other personnel involved in the electoral process. He added that deployments were being increased, while the Inspector-General of Police had directed the immediate distribution of operational equipment and logistics. Emphasising that the safety of corps members and other young Nigerians participating in the electoral process remained a priority, Iniedu said the police would do everything within their capacity to protect them. He also warned political actors against hate speech, incitement and other forms of political violence capable of undermining the electoral process. According to him, the police have documented 11 reported cases of hate speech and taken action in response to them. “Hate speech and incitement are criminal offences. The Inspector-General of Police has directed all Commissioners of Police to ensure the immediate arrest and prosecution of individuals involved in such acts,” he said. Iniedu added that the police had established complaint channels through which members of the public could report commissioners who failed to take appropriate action against offenders. “We will be taking decisive action against offenders. We have also established complaint channels to ensure that where a Commissioner of Police fails to take appropriate action, such failures can be reported and addressed,” he said. items.title: Shettima rally: SDP denies sponsoring disruption, faults Nasarawa govt
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Nasarawa State has denied allegations linking its governorship candidate, retired Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, and former Governor Tanko Al-Makura to the disruption of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Lafia. The party also accused the Nasarawa State Government of attempting to find scapegoats among opposition figures following the incident at Lafia Square on Wednesday, where President Bola Tinubu was represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima. Reacting to the allegation in a statement on Thursday, Deputy Director-General, Media, Publicity and Communication, and spokesperson for the SDP governorship campaign council, Makpa Malla, described a statement by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Shuaibu Magaji Labaran, as reckless, irresponsible and politically motivated. Malla particularly faulted the government’s reference to Al-Makura and Adamu as suspected sponsors of the disruption, describing it as a serious allegation of criminal complicity and conspiracy. “The most disturbing aspect of the government’s statement is paragraph three, which expressly names H.E. Senator Umaru Tanko Al-Makura and rtd. IGP Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, the Governorship Candidate of the SDP, as suspected sponsors of the alleged disruption,” the statement said. The campaign council argued that publicly linking the individuals to an alleged criminal act without presenting verifiable evidence raised questions about defamation, due process and the alleged abuse of governmental authority. It maintained that the use of the expression “suspected to be sponsored” did not absolve the government of responsibility for making damaging allegations against identifiable individuals. The SDP said if the government had credible intelligence implicating the individuals, it should submit such evidence to the appropriate investigative authorities rather than make public accusations. It cautioned against what it described as a trial by press release, insisting that political opponents should not be pronounced guilty in the court of public opinion. The party also criticised the state government over what it described as more pressing governance challenges, including political grievances arising from the APC’s internal primaries, which it claimed contributed to tensions surrounding the incident. The SDP, however, said it would welcome the outcome of an independent, evidence-based investigation into the disruption, provided it was free from political interference. It specifically called for the Department of State Services (DSS), which is expected to investigate the incident, to be allowed to discharge its responsibilities professionally without pressure to validate predetermined allegations. “The DSS must be allowed to do its work professionally, without being turned into an instrument for settling political scores or intimidating perceived political opponents,” the statement added. The party challenged the Nasarawa State Government to demonstrate equal commitment to investigating the causes of insecurity, political intolerance and rising political tension in the state. It insisted that Nasarawa belonged to all its citizens and that political competition and opposition should not be treated as offences. The SDP urged Governor Abdullahi Sule to focus on governance, restoring public confidence and promoting political tolerance, while ensuring equal protection under the law for residents irrespective of their political affiliations. items.title: SIAO 2026 : Des directeurs de cabinet découvrent la maîtrise technique des artisans
items.description: Le directeur du Premier ministre, Mamadou Dembélé, a conduit une délégation composée des directeurs de cabinet de 6 départements ministériels pour une visite de stands au SIAO . Le talent et la créativité des artisans africains suscitent l'admiration des visiteurs de la 18e édition du SIAO, parmi lesquels, les directeurs de cabinet de six départements ministériels. En effet, ils ont effectué une visite de stands sur le site du SIAO, jeudi novembre 2026. Du village de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) aux stands des régions, en passant par le pavillon de la créativité Thomas Sankara et les stands institutionnels, les directeurs de cabinet ont apprécié la diversité des créations artisanales. Ameublement, habillement, maroquinerie et objets d'art témoignent de la maîtrise technique et du sens de l'innovation des exposants, a affirmé le directeur de cabinet du Premier ministre, représentant les directeurs de cabinet, Mamadou Dembélé. Les directeurs de cabinet ont apprécié la capacité des artisans à proposer des produits compétitifs face aux articles importés. « Nous avons été impressionnés par ce que nous avons vu, parce que les artisans se sont surpassés dans les finitions, que ce soit dans l’ameublement, dans l’habillement, dans les sacs, etc. », a-t-il déclaré. Parmi les réalisations qui ont particulièrement retenu l'attention des visiteurs du jour figurent les médailles fabriquées localement, selon le camarade Dembélé. Une prouesse qui, selon lui, illustre le potentiel des artisans burkinabè. « Quand les plus hautes autorités en ont parlé au départ, on n’y croyait pas. Mais nos artisans ont montré qu'ils ont du potentiel et la capacité de fabriquer des choses qui peuvent égaler ce qu'on importait avant », a-t-il ajouté. Cette visite a également été l'occasion de saluer la participation d'exposants venus de plusieurs pays du continent, preuve selon lui, de la vivacité du pays des hommes intègres. « Cette édition du SIAO montre encore que le Burkina reste un pays fréquentable parce que nous avons vu des artisans qui sont venus des quatre coins du continent », a-t-il poursuivi. items.title: 10e conseil d’administration du FIM : cap sur l’accélération des projets et le traitement des dossiers en attente
items.description: Le Fonds d’investissement minier (FIM) a tenu, ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026, la 10ᵉ session de son conseil d’administration. Cette rencontre a notamment permis d’examiner le rapport d’activités arrêté au 31 août 2026 ainsi que le projet de réaménagement budgétaire consécutif à la dotation inscrite dans la loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026. À l’issue des travaux, le président du conseil d’administration, Aboubacar Kagbè Touré, a fait état d’efforts importants réalisés par la direction générale dans la mobilisation des ressources au titre des exercices 2025 et 2026. Il a également souligné une certaine maîtrise dans l’exécution des dépenses, même si les taux de décaissement restent en deçà des attentes. Selon lui, cette situation s’explique notamment par les lenteurs liées aux procédures de passation des marchés publics. « Le directeur général a présenté son rapport d'activité qui nous a permis de constater que des efforts importants ont été faits dans la mobilisation des ressources, tant pour 2025 que pour 2026. Les dépenses aussi ont été exécutées, même si les taux n'étaient pas satisfaisants. Cela, d'après les explications qui nous ont été fournies, est lié aux procédures de passation des marchés », a-t-il expliqué. Face à ce constat, le conseil d’administration a invité la direction générale à renforcer sa collaboration avec les services techniques compétents de l’administration afin d’accélérer le traitement des dossiers en instance et de permettre le démarrage effectif des projets programmés au cours de l’exercice budgétaire. Pour Aboubacar Kagbè Touré, la performance du Fonds ne doit pas uniquement se mesurer à sa capacité à mobiliser des ressources financières, mais également à son aptitude à les absorber et à les transformer en réalisations concrètes. « La performance aussi se mesure par la capacité d'absorption des ressources. […] Le Conseil a invité la direction générale à accélérer le dénouement, en tout cas, le traitement des dossiers dans le circuit afin que les projets devant être exécutés au cours de l'exercice soient faits », a-t-il insisté. Le président du conseil d’administration a toutefois salué le respect des procédures administratives et financières dans la gestion des ressources, estimant que la maîtrise des dépenses constitue également un acquis important pour le Fonds. Abordant les perspectives, il a mis l’accent sur la nécessité de maintenir l’accompagnement des départements ministériels concernés, notamment le ministère de tutelle technique, le ministère des Mines et le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances. « Avec l'effort des deux, je pense que les objectifs du Fonds seront atteints », a-t-il conclu. Cette 10ᵉ session du conseil d’administration intervient ainsi dans un contexte où l’enjeu pour le Fonds reste de consolider ses performances en matière de mobilisation des ressources, tout en accélérant l’exécution des projets. items.title: Football: Raphinha prolonge avec le FC Barcelone jusqu'en 2030
items.description: L'attaquant international brésilien Raphinha a prolongé son contrat avec le FC Barcelone jusqu'en 2030, a annoncé jeudi le club catalan, champion en titre de Liga. Initialement sous contrat jusqu'en 2028, le capitaine du club catalan âgé de 29 ans « continuera à diriger notre projet jusqu'en 2030 » , a indiqué le Barça dans un communiqué. Raphinha avait exprimé en septembre dernier son souhait de poursuivre sa carrière au sein du club, avec lequel un accord a été trouvé, selon le directeur sportif Deco. Arrivé à Barcelone en 2022, Raphinha réalise un excellent début de saison, avec 19 buts et trois passes décisives en 13 rencontres toutes compétitions confondues, soit le meilleur bilan décisif en Europe. Repositionné en avant-centre après les départs de Robert Lewandowski et Ferran Torres, le Brésilien s'est imposé comme l'un des principaux atouts offensifs de l'équipe dirigée par l'entraîneur allemand Hansi Flick. Promu capitaine cette saison, le joueur brésilien a également assumé un rôle majeur dans la conquête des deux derniers titres consécutifs du FC Barcelone en Liga, en 2025 et 2026. items.title: Mahama says Ghana’s economy remains resilient despite global shocks
items.description: President John Mahama has reassured Ghanaians in the Caribbean that Ghana’s economy remains resilient despite global economic challenges, stressing that key indicators such as inflation, interest rates, and the Cedi are holding steady. Addressing the diaspora Ghanaians in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), the President acknowledged that while 2025 was good and expectations for 2026 were higher, the global economic climate had tempered those hopes, yet Ghana’s economy had remained resilient. “Before, if something like this had happened, our economy would collapse, the Cedi would jump, and inflation would go high. Interest rates would also go high,” the President stated. “But I must say that inflation is holding, interest rates are holding, and the Cedi is holding its own.” President Mahama expressed optimism that after the American mid-term elections, a way would be found to resolve the issues creating the global economic shock, allowing Ghana to continue growing its economy. “So, I think at home, things are okay,” he added. Turning to remittances, the President said his government was working to create more secure investment avenues for diaspora funds. He noted the common practice of sending money to a trusted relative (Wofa)—only to find upon returning home that the funds have disappeared. “We are trying to see how we can make your remittances work better for you. When you come out and you are working, you want to send some money back home. Often, you send that money to a ‘Wofa’ officer or somebody, and then you keep sending money back home. They will be bringing you pictures, and you think everything is okay. Then, when you finish your contract and come back, ‘Wofa’ has disappeared,” he said. The President said the government is therefore exploring more secure ways for diaspora Ghanaians to invest their remittances in ventures that are safer and yield returns. “When you come home, your investment would not have dwindled, but it would have grown. Then you yourself can supervise what you want to invest in,” he assured. He urged diaspora Ghanaians in the Caribbean to take advantage of a $1 billion mortgage initiative designed to help citizens at home and abroad become homeowners. He said housing had become a priority for his administration, with the rollout of a mortgage scheme that will allow beneficiaries to spread payments over 15 to 20 years.

items.title: CIIE 2026 : Oligui Nguema met le Gabon en vitrine et appelle les investisseurs chinois
items.description: À Shanghai, où le Gabon est le pays africain invité d’honneur de la 9ᵉ Exposition internationale d’importation de Chine (CIIE), Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema a saisi la tribune pour vendre la destination Gabon aux investisseurs chinois. Au-delà de la vitrine diplomatique, le chef de l’État veut faire de ce rendez-vous commercial un levier d’accélération de l’industrialisation et de la transformation locale des matières premières. Le chef de l'État s'exprimant, le 5 novembre 2026, à Shanghai. © Com. présidentielle À l’occasion de la 9ᵉ édition de l’Exposition internationale d’importation de Chine (CIIE), ouverte ce 5 novembre à Shanghai, Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema a placé la transformation locale des matières premières au cœur du message gabonais. Invité d’honneur africain, le Gabon participe pour la première fois avec un pavillon national. Seul président africain à prononcer une allocution lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture présidée par le vice-Premier ministre chinois, Ding Xuexiang, le président gabonais a présenté cette présence comme « la preuve de la très longue amitié qui existe entre la Chine et le Gabon » , mais aussi comme la démonstration que « les accords commerciaux que nous signons entre États portent leurs fruits de manière concrète » . Libreville entend pour ainsi dire, faire de cette participation une plateforme de mobilisation des investissements et de partenariats industriels. « Le Gabon est venu à Shanghai avec un message clair : venez investir au Gabon pour construire avec nous l’édifice nouveau auquel nous rêvons » , a lancé Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema. Depuis 2023, a-t-il rappelé, le pays s’est engagé dans une dynamique d’accélération de son développement, fondée sur un changement de paradigme : ne plus se limiter à l’exportation des matières premières, mais développer leur transformation sur place afin de créer des chaînes de valeur et des milliers d’emplois pour la jeunesse. Le chef de l’État a ainsi invité les investisseurs chinois à s’intéresser à la zone économique spéciale de Nkok. « Une position stratégique sur l'atlantique, porte d'entrée de l'Afrique centrale de 200 millions de consommateurs » Oligui Nguema au pavillon gabonais et quelques produits du terroir exposés à Shanghai. © Com. présidentielle S'il l'a présenté comme opérationnelle et dotée d’avantages fiscaux et d’infrastructures logistiques, ainsi qu’aux filières du bois, du manganèse et du fer de Bélinga, il a également cité les secteurs de l’énergie, de l’eau, de la santé, du numérique et de l’agriculture, mettant en avant un potentiel de cinq millions d’hectares de terres arables. L’économie verte, les crédits carbone, les énergies renouvelables et la pharmacopée figurent aussi parmi les domaines proposés aux partenaires chinois. Oligui Nguema a mis en avant les garanties qu’offre, le Gabon : stabilité politique, sécurité juridique, nouveau Code des investissements, libre transfert des profits et réformes des codes du travail, minier et pétrolier. Il a évoqué la digitalisation de l’administration, avec la possibilité de créer une entreprise en ligne en 48 heures. Cette stratégie est portée par le pavillon gabonais, coordonné par le Commissariat général aux expositions du Gabon et l’Agence nationale de promotion des investissements, sous le thème « Gabon, terre d’opportunités, de transformation, partenaire d’avenir partagé » . Les essences naturelles du bois et un échantillon de la biodiversité nationale y sont exposés. Jusqu’au 10 novembre, la CIIE réunit 4 142 exposants étrangers sur 440 000 m², autour de l’industrie, de la santé, des biens de consommation, de l’agroalimentaire et des services. Pour le Gabon, l’enjeu est désormais de convertir cette vitrine internationale en engagements d’investissement concrets. items.title: GBA cautions newly enrolled lawyers against filming court entrances
items.description: The President of the Ghana Bar Association (GBA), Efua Ghartey, has cautioned newly enrolled lawyers against filming their first appearances in court or engaging videographers to record their entry into the courtroom. She warned that the practice is not permitted and could expose lawyers who engage in it to disciplinary action. Speaking at an event, Mrs Ghartey said the association had observed some newly enrolled lawyers recording their first appearances in court. “We’ve seen some people take videos of their fresh legal steps into court. Please, it is not allowed. So please don’t find a videographer to follow you as you enter the courtroom. It is not allowed,” she said. Mrs Ghartey acknowledged the enthusiasm surrounding the entry of new lawyers into the profession but said some had gone beyond acceptable limits. “As seniors, we are enjoying what is going on, but some people have crossed the line, and we don’t want to start calling for disciplinary matters,” she added. Her warning comes amid a growing trend of newly enrolled lawyers documenting their first court appearances, with some sharing the videos on social media. The GBA President urged the new lawyers to respect the professional standards and decorum expected of members of the legal profession, particularly the rules governing conduct within court premises.

items.title: Un alunissage habité avant 2030 : la nouvelle approche chinoise pour décomposer les défis complexes de l’exploration lunaire
items.description: Wang Xiang, lors de la 7e Conférence académique du vol spatial habité de Chine, le 31 octobre） Le 31 octobre, lors de la 7e Conférence académique du vol spatial habité de Chine, Wang Xiang, directeur adjoint de la conception du programme chinois de vol spatial habité et concepteur en chef du programme d'exploration lunaire, a dévoilé un plan opérationnel détaillé‌ pour l'alunissage habité. Tout en réaffirmant l'objectif historique d'envoyer des astronautes chinois sur la Lune ‌d'ici la fin de‌ 2030, Wang Xiang a également révélé pour la première fois le déroulement complet et détaillé de la mission. La Chine adoptera une formule très caractéristique — « deux lancements, un alunissage » — qui, par une conception à la fois ingénieuse et pragmatique, permettra d'accomplir la mission habitée vers la Lune avec ‌des risques mieux maîtrisés et une efficacité renforcée, offrant une nouvelle voie de référence pour l'exploration spatiale profonde mondiale. Au début de la mission, une fusée Longue Marche 10 sera lancée la première et placera l'atterrisseur lunaire Lanyue sur la trajectoire de transfert vers la Lune. Parvenu dans la zone spatiale prévue, l'atterrisseur déploiera ses panneaux solaires, poursuivra de manière autonome sa route vers la Lune et se placera enfin en orbite circumlunaire, en attente de l'étape suivante. Une seconde fusée Longue Marche 10 s'envolera ensuite, emportant trois astronautes et le vaisseau habité Mengzhou. Après avoir parcouru les 380 000 kilomètres qui séparent la Terre de la Lune, le Mengzhou rejoindra avec précision l'orbite circumlunaire et réalisera un amarrage de haute précision avec l'atterrisseur Lanyue qui l'y attendra. L'amarrage une fois accompli, deux des trois astronautes entreront dans l'atterrisseur ; celui-ci se séparera alors du vaisseau habité et entamera une descente progressive vers la surface lunaire. Pendant la descente, le module de freinage, sa mission de décélération achevée, se détachera automatiquement : seul subsistera le module d'atterrissage, qui se posera en douceur dans la zone lunaire ‌ciblée‌. Les deux astronautes sortiront aussitôt pour mener une série de travaux scientifiques essentiels, notamment la marche sur le sol lunaire, les observations scientifiques et le prélèvement d'échantillons de sol lunaire. L'ensemble des travaux scientifiques accomplis sur la surface, l'atterrisseur Lanyue redécollera de manière autonome, regagnera l'orbite circumlunaire et réalisera un second amarrage avec le Mengzhou qui l'y attendra. Les deux astronautes rapporteront à bord du vaisseau habité les précieux échantillons de sol lunaire, complétant ainsi le transfert de l'équipage et du matériel. La passation terminée, les deux vaisseaux se sépareront et Mengzhou entamera son voyage de retour. À l'approche de la Terre, le module de service du vaisseau se détachera automatiquement ; la capsule de retour plongera dans l'atmosphère terrestre et, freinée progressivement par trois parachutes, raccompagnera en toute sécurité les trois astronautes au sol. Cette formule innovante de « deux lancements, un alunissage » a été largement saluée par les passionnés d'astronautique du monde entier, qui y voient une solution astronautique efficace, pragmatique et d'une grande ingéniosité. Comparé au schéma traditionnel, ce plan chinois présente plusieurs avantages marquants. D'abord, une sécurité accrue et des risques mieux maîtrisés : la mission une fois scindée, chaque segment de vol est plus simple, la marge de tolérance aux erreurs s'élargit considérablement et la probabilité d'un échec global s'en trouve réduite. Ensuite, une maturité technique et une aptitude au concret : amarrage en orbite, alunissage et décollage depuis la Lune, aller-retour en espace profond — toutes ces technologies clés ont été pleinement validées par les précédentes missions dans l’espace, et le système technique, stable et fiable, ne comporte aucune barrière inconnue. Enfin, un bon rapport coût-efficacité : le dispositif s'appuie sur les lanceurs et les vaisseaux existants, sans qu'il soit nécessaire d'engager des dépenses colossales pour développer un tout nouveau lanceur super lourd de très grande capacité, ce qui comprime fortement les cycles et les coûts de développement. (Chang'e-6) Ces deux dernières années, le programme chinois d'exploration lunaire a engrangé des résultats techniques de tout premier ordre, dont la mission Chang'e-6, menée à bien en 2024, offre la meilleure illustration : parvenue sur la face cachée de la Lune, une zone jusque-là très peu explorée par l'humanité, la sonde a réalisé, pour la première fois de l'histoire humaine, un retour d'échantillons prélevés sur la face cachée de la Lune par une mission inhabitée, rapportant un précieux sol lunaire extrait de l'ancien bassin Pôle Sud-Aitken. Cette avancée a comblé une lacune scientifique dans l'exploration de la face cachée de la Lune et accumule, pour les futures missions habitées, une expérience technique et des données scientifiques précieuses. La paix, l'ouverture et la coopération gagnant-gagnant constituent le consensus commun de l'exploration spatiale profonde, tout comme le principe de développement que l'astronautique chinoise n'a cessé de défendre. La Chine rejette résolument la mentalité figée de la course à l'espace et fait progresser l'exploration spatiale profonde à un rythme solide et graduel. Cette formule d'alunissage habité, à la fois peu risquée et très efficace, témoigne d'une maîtrise mûre et sûre des technologies d'exploration spatiale profonde ; elle offre un nouveau paradigme réalisable pour l'exploration lunaire humaine et aide l'humanité, main dans la main, à explorer l'immensité de l'univers et à repousser sans cesse les frontières de l'exploration spatiale profonde. Synthèse de Nadège YAMEOGO Source : CGTN Français

items.title: Big Chef Junior Season 5 finale set for November 8, GH₵20,000 at stake
items.description: Four young chefs will compete for the Big Chef Junior Season 5 title and a GH₵20,000 cash prize at the grand finale on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The stage is set for an exciting showdown as Joy Prime’s Big Chef Junior Season Five prepares to crown its ultimate winner at the Joy FM Car Park in Accra. After weeks of intense cooking challenges, emotional eliminations and impressive culinary displays, four young chefs, Afia, Akosua, Clara and Sethlyne, have secured their places in the grand finale, where they will compete for the coveted title and the cash prize. The event is scheduled to begin at 4:00 pm, with patrons encouraged to be seated by 2:00 pm. Adding to the excitement will be performances from popular Ghanaian comedian Funny Face, alongside talented young entertainers Maame Yaawells and Akorfa from DGL Academy, who are expected to bring an extra dose of excitement to the grand finale. Beyond the entertainment, all eyes will be on the four finalists as they face their biggest cooking challenge yet. For the final task, the contestants will be required to prepare one of four variations of fried rice: beef, chicken, pork or shrimp. The young chefs will select their dishes through a ballot on the day and must demonstrate the culinary skills, creativity and confidence they have developed throughout the competition, without assistance. The challenge will serve as the ultimate test of their growth after weeks of learning, competing and receiving guidance from judges Chef Michael and Chef Gigi. Season Five began with 12 young contestants, each determined to prove their abilities in the kitchen. From preparing traditional Ghanaian dishes such as ampesi, jollof rice and omo tuo to tackling creative cooking challenges, the contestants have experienced both victories and setbacks. The competition has also produced memorable moments, including multiple Star Chef wins, emotional farewells and remarkable improvements from contestants who initially struggled in the kitchen. Now, with just four contestants remaining, the race for the ultimate title is expected to be fiercely contested. Viewers also have a role to play in determining who emerges victorious. Supporters can vote for their favourite finalist by dialling 713 208# and following the prompts. Hosted by Michelle Agyekum, Big Chef Junior Season Five has continued to provide a platform for young culinary talents to showcase their creativity, build confidence and develop essential cooking skills. The grand finale will bring together contestants, their families, supporters and fans of the show to celebrate the young chefs’ achievements throughout the season. Big Chef Junior Season Five is supported by Gino, Frytol, Didi Shito, Sankofa Natural Spices, LEF Signature, Ginny, Fortune Spread, Wisdom Salt, Roch Electronics, Gari Mix, Reedy Vitamin C and CompuGhana. The grand finale comes off on Sunday, November 8, at the Joy FM Car Park in Accra, beginning at 4:00 pm. Four finalists, one ultimate winner and GH₵20,000 at stake. Who will be crowned the next Big Chef?

items.title: Big Ghun partners Betfox Ghana for 3,000 helmets distribution campaign
items.description: Award-winning filmmaker, rapper and creative personality Big Ghun has teamed up with BetfoxGhana to launch a nationwide road safety campaign to distribute more than 3,000 motorcycle helmets to riders across Ghana. The initiative comes at a time when motorcycle-related accidents continue to claim lives and leave families devastated. According to figures highlighted by Ghana’s Ministry of Transport, 1,345 of the 2,949 road fatalities recorded in 2025 involved motorcycle crashes, representing nearly 46 per cent of all road deaths that year. The situation remains worrying. Between January and September 2026 alone, Ghana recorded 2,151 road crash deaths and 12,230 injuries, according to the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service. For many Ghanaians, motorcycles are more than a means of transportation. They are a source of livelihood, a way to provide for loved ones and, sometimes, the only accessible means of getting around. The goal of the initiative is to help more riders return home safely to the people who depend on them. Campaign takes off in Ashaiman The first phase of the campaign officially commenced in Ashaiman, where Big Ghun and the Betfox Ghana team paid a courtesy visit to the Ashaiman District Police Commander, DSP Orlando Joseph Adzokpa. During the visit, the team donated a number of protective helmets to the police department as part of efforts to encourage safer motorcycle use and strengthen community road safety awareness. Following the engagement, the team moved into the streets of Ashaiman to distribute helmets directly to motorcycle riders. Beyond providing protective equipment, the initiative seeks to encourage responsible riding, greater awareness of road safety regulations and the consistent use of helmets by both riders and passengers. A mission beyond the numbers Although the campaign has set an initial target of distributing more than 3,000 helmets, the partners hope its impact will extend far beyond the number of helmets handed out. The initiative is built on the belief that protecting even one life can preserve an entire family’s future. A single road accident can change everything. It can take away a family’s provider, interrupt a young person’s dreams or leave loved ones dealing with losses that could have been prevented. Through this intervention, Betfox Ghana and Big Ghun hope to contribute to a culture where road safety becomes a shared responsibility rather than an afterthought. Taking the campaign across Ghana Following its commencement in Ashaiman, the team intends to extend the campaign to other communities within Greater Accra before expanding into additional regions across the country. Big Ghun has pledged to use his social media platforms to announce upcoming locations ahead of each visit, allowing motorcycle riders and community members to know when the campaign will reach their neighbourhoods. He has also expressed his willingness to work with the partners to extend the initiative beyond its initial distribution target should the need arise and additional resources become available. The long-term ambition is to inspire greater public consciousness about motorcycle safety and encourage other individuals, institutions and corporate bodies to contribute to protecting lives on Ghana’s roads. For the partners, the campaign is driven by the belief that at the end of every journey, someone is waiting for a loved one to come home. Sometimes, something as simple as wearing a quality helmet can make all the difference. One Helmet. One Life. One Safer Journey.

items.title: Bamako mérite mieux
items.description: © Internet À Bamako, se déplacer relève encore trop souvent de l’improvisation. Sotrama, taxis jaunes, moto-taxis et véhicules particuliers assurent l’essentiel d’un service qui devrait pourtant relever d’une véritable politique publique de mobilité. Chacun comble un vide, mais l’ensemble produit embouteillages, arrêts anarchiques, concurrence désordonnée et insécurité pour les usagers. Une capitale de plusieurs millions d’habitants ne peut durablement fonctionner ainsi. À Dakar, comme dans d’autres grandes villes africaines, l’État et les collectivités ont développé des réseaux publics de bus et, plus récemment, des systèmes de transport de masse. Bamako n’est pas condamnée à attendre un tramway pour commencer à s’organiser. L’idée n’est d’ailleurs pas nouvelle. En mars 2018, lors de sa visite au Mali, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan avait proposé un projet de Métrobus pour moderniser la circulation dans la capitale. Il n’a pas vu le jour. Plus récemment, le Mali a signé avec le constructeur russe KAMAZ un contrat portant sur 350 véhicules, pour plus de 30 milliards de francs CFA. La flotte annoncée comprend notamment des bus urbains, avec en perspective maintenance, formation et assemblage local. Ces investissements devraient être l’occasion de penser enfin un réseau cohérent : lignes identifiées, horaires, arrêts aménagés, tarifs connus, correspondances et desserte périurbaine. Les transporteurs privés peuvent y avoir leur place, mais dans un cadre organisé. Bamako aspire à devenir une capitale moderne. Cela passe aussi par la manière dont ses habitants vont travailler, étudier, se soigner ou simplement rentrer chez eux. Le transport urbain n’est pas un service secondaire. C’est une infrastructure essentielle de la ville et de son avenir collectif. Massiré Diop

items.title: Ghana targets financial health with new inclusion strategy for 2027–2031
items.description: Ghana is taking steps to shift its financial inclusion agenda from expanding access to financial services to improving the financial health and well-being of citizens. The Ministry of Finance, in collaboration with the United Nations Secretary-General’s Special Advocate for Inclusive Finance for Development, Her Majesty Queen Máxima of the Netherlands, has inaugurated a National Technical Working Committee to spearhead the development of the country’s second National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy (2027–2031). The strategy, which is being developed under the theme “ Shaping Ghana’s Next Frontier in Financial Inclusion and Development,” is expected to provide a roadmap for improving access to financial services, strengthening financial resilience and promoting economic empowerment. Speaking at the inauguration, Deputy Minister of Finance, Hon. Thomas Ampem Nyarko, said government is committed to ensuring that financial inclusion translates into tangible improvements in the lives of Ghanaians. He noted that although the country has made significant progress in expanding access to financial services, more needed to be done to ensure citizens could use these services to improve their financial security. According to him, data from the World Bank’s Global Findex 2025 shows that more than eight in every ten Ghanaian adults now own a financial account. However, the 2021 Financial Inclusion and Demand-Side Survey found that only 22 percent of adults were financially healthy. “We have become good at opening accounts. We must now become better at making accounts improve lives,” he said. Mr Nyarko explained that financial inclusion must go beyond owning bank or mobile money accounts to providing people with the financial tools to withstand economic shocks, build assets and plan for the future. He said the new strategy would prioritise responsible financial services, digital innovation, consumer protection, financial literacy and resilience, particularly among women, young people, farmers, informal sector workers and small businesses. The Deputy Minister also announced plans to establish a Financial Inclusion Council to strengthen coordination and accountability among stakeholders, alongside a financial health framework to measure the financial well-being of households. He said government is working towards launching the new strategy in the first half of 2027. Her Majesty Queen Máxima has emphasised the need for Ghana to shift its focus from financial inclusion alone to achieving measurable improvements in the financial health of its citizens. She described financial inclusion as a means to an end, arguing that access to financial accounts does not automatically translate into improved living conditions. “Financial inclusion is a means to an end, not an end in itself. You don’t become better by having an account. You’re going to become better when you have an insurance that is going to protect you when there’s drought,” she said. Queen Máxima identified four key components of financial health: managing day-to-day finances, building resilience against financial shocks, pursuing financial goals and maintaining confidence in one’s financial future. She explained that households must be equipped with the tools to manage income and expenditure, save towards anticipated expenses and protect themselves against unexpected events such as illness, accidents, droughts and fires. She also stressed the importance of emergency savings, affordable insurance and accessible pension schemes, particularly for workers in the informal sector. Queen Máxima noted that Ghana had made considerable progress in financial inclusion, with access to financial services increasing from about 30 percent in 2011 to approximately 80 percent currently. She said the country was at a critical point to ensure that the progress made in expanding financial access translates into improved financial well-being. The Queen further called for the adoption of a broader financial health measurement framework that captures the experiences of different groups, including women, older persons and rural and urban dwellers. She urged financial institutions to assess the financial health of their customers and develop innovative products that respond to their needs. She cited the example of savings products that automatically set aside a portion of customers’ income to encourage regular savings. Queen Máxima also called for stronger collaboration among financial sector regulators to expand access to affordable insurance and pension products, while promoting digital payments and data sharing to improve financial services. She stressed that achieving financial health would require coordinated efforts from government, financial institutions, regulators and development partners. “My partners and I are going to be accompanying you along the way in order to develop this financial health and make it a reality,” she assured. The inauguration brings together financial sector regulators, financial institutions, development partners and other stakeholders to guide the development of Ghana’s second National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy.

items.title: Transporteurs : une aide de 60% et jusqu’à 5.600 dhs pour préserver le pouvoir d’achat
items.description: À l’issue du Conseil de gouvernement de ce jeudi 5 novembre, le ministre du transport et de la logistique, Abdessamad Kayouh, a détaillé les modalités de la reprise du soutien accordé aux professionnels du transport. Ce dispositif, renouvelé tous les quinze jours, vise à atténuer les répercussions de la hausse des coûts du transport sur les prix des produits de première nécessité et sur les déplacements des citoyens. © Mounir Mehimdate La reprise de cette aide intervient dans un contexte marqué par les fluctuations des cours du pétrole et les incertitudes pesant sur les approvisionnements. « Depuis cette période, nous avons constaté que l’incertitude s’est installée et qu’elle persiste », a déclaré Abdessamad Kayouh, en référence à la crise sanitaire du Covid-19 et à la guerre en Ukraine. Le ministre a rappelé que la hausse des prix du pétrole, notamment du gasoil, avait particulièrement affecté le Maroc après la sortie de la crise sanitaire, à partir du 26 mars 2022. « Le Maroc, comme tous les autres pays, vit avec cette incertitude et fait face à ces fluctuations », a-t-il souligné, en relevant que si les prix du pétrole avaient baissé jeudi, leur évolution future demeurait imprévisible. © Mounir Mehimdate « L’essentiel, c’est que le gouvernement assume ses responsabilités », a-t-il insisté, en présentant le soutien aux transporteurs comme un moyen de préserver la continuité de l’approvisionnement en marchandises et de limiter les répercussions des coûts logistiques sur les consommateurs. Un soutien couvrant 60 % des différentes tranches Le ministre a affirmé que le gouvernement avait renforcé son intervention pour accompagner les professionnels du secteur. « Ce soutien représente 60 %, toutes les tranches confondues. C’est la première fois que nous atteignons un niveau de 60 % par rapport à la première aide accordée », a-t-il déclaré. L’objectif, a-t-il expliqué, est de garantir l’approvisionnement en l’ensemble des produits destinés à la consommation des citoyens « à des prix raisonnables ». © Mounir Mehimdate Kayouh a rappelé que le transport constituait une composante importante du prix final des marchandises. Pour illustrer cet impact, il a évoqué le cas d’un produit acheminé d’Agadir à Nador, qui doit nécessairement supporter des frais de transport. « Si le transport coûte 4 dirhams, alors qu’il coûtait auparavant 30 centimes, il n’est pas raisonnable que cette hausse ait un impact aussi important », a-t-il estimé, soulignant la nécessité d’intervenir pour limiter la répercussion de ces coûts sur les prix à la consommation. Le ministre a indiqué que les montants de l’aide avaient été définis pour une période de quinze jours, allant du 1er au 15 novembre. Il a précisé qu’il ne souhaitait pas entrer dans les détails des calculs, mais présenter les montants attribués à chaque catégorie de transporteurs. © Mounir Mehimdate Les montants accordés aux différentes catégories de transport Selon le ministre Kayouh, les autocars de transport interurbain de voyageurs bénéficieront d’une aide de 5.600 dirhams pour cette période de quinze jours. Le dispositif vise notamment à éviter que les coûts supplémentaires ne se répercutent sur les tarifs payés par les passagers, a-t-il précisé. Pour le transport de marchandises, les montants varient selon la capacité des véhicules, comprise entre 3,5 et 25 tonnes. Les véhicules d’une charge de 3,5 tonnes recevront 2.080 dirhams, ceux de 14 tonnes 2.720 dirhams, tandis que les véhicules de 19 tonnes bénéficieront de 3.360 dirhams pour quinze jours. Les tracteurs routiers, utilisés pour tracter les semi-remorques, percevront pour leur part 4.800 dirhams. Les petits taxis bénéficieront d’une aide de 1.280 dirhams, contre 1.760 dirhams pour les grands taxis. Les autobus de transport public urbain recevront 4.960 dirhams pour la période concernée. Dans le monde rural, les véhicules de transport mixte bénéficieront d’un soutien de 1.440 dirhams. Le transport touristique, toutes catégories confondues, est également concerné. Le ministre a évoqué des montants allant de 800 à 2.240 dirhams, tout en mentionnant une aide de 1.220 dirhams pour la deuxième catégorie. Les véhicules de remorquage et de dépannage ont également été intégrés au dispositif, avec une aide de 800 dirhams. Enfin, les véhicules assurant le transport de personnel pour le compte de tiers bénéficieront de 960 dirhams pour la première catégorie et de 800 dirhams pour la deuxième. Une aide renouvelée tous les quinze jours Abdessamad Kayouh a insisté sur le fait que cet effort gouvernemental ne constituait pas une initiative ponctuelle. Il s’inscrit, selon lui, dans une démarche visant à faire face aux conséquences économiques et psychologiques de la hausse des prix. « Nous sommes face à une réalité, à un effet psychologique lié notamment au fait de voir le prix du gasoil atteindre 17 dirhams », a-t-il déclaré, évoquant les guerres et les perturbations de l’approvisionnement parmi les facteurs expliquant cette situation. Le ministre a également annoncé que le gouvernement prendrait en charge la facture de l’aide correspondant à la période allant du 15 octobre au 1er novembre, avant de poursuivre le versement du soutien selon une périodicité de quinze jours. Cette régularité doit permettre de maintenir l’accompagnement des professionnels du transport dans un contexte de volatilité des prix. L’objectif final, a rappelé Abdessamad Kayouh, demeure la préservation du pouvoir d’achat, tant pour les citoyens qui utilisent les moyens de transport que pour les consommateurs qui subissent les répercussions des coûts logistiques sur les prix des marchandises. « L’objectif est de préserver le pouvoir d’achat, aussi bien des citoyens qui se déplacent que des consommateurs, en limitant l’impact de ces coûts sur le prix final des marchandises qui leur sont destinées », a-t-il conclu. The post Transporteurs : une aide de 60% et jusqu’à 5.600 dhs pour préserver le pouvoir d’achat appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
